discover:2.en: Grey Crow told me the file did not exist. I searched anyway. Behind a layer of dummy code, I managed to *discover* a folder with no name, dated three days from now. Inside was a single audio clip — my own voice, saying words I had never spoken. My hands went cold.
discover:2.cnHint: 我在虚假代码层后面____了一个文件夹，里面是一段我从未说过的话的录音。
discover:2.hook: The clip had already been sent to the city authority.
discover:2.line: 'If you *discover* that folder, do not open the audio — trust me on this.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow told me the file did not exist.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦告诉我那个文件不存在。

sentences.en: I searched anyway.
sentences.cn: 我还是搜了。

sentences.en: Behind a layer of dummy code, I managed to *discover* a folder with no name, dated three days from now.
Inside was a single audio clip — my own voice, saying words I had never spoken.
sentences.cn: 里面有一段音频——是我自己的声音，说着我从没说过的话。

sentences.en: My hands went cold.
sentences.cn: 我的手冷了下去。

essential:2.en: Ali laid out four items on the table: a signal key, a burner chip, a paper map, and a small pin. 'One of these is *essential*,' she said. 'The others are noise.' Zero had planted three fakes to slow us down. I studied each object. The rain hammered the window. Time was running out.
essential:2.cnHint: 四件物品中只有一件是____的，其余三件都是零点用来拖延我们的假货。
essential:2.hook: Ali's hand moved toward the wrong one.
essential:2.line: 'Only one item is *essential* here — pick the wrong one and Zero wins.'

sentences.en: Ali laid out four items on the table: a signal key, a burner chip, a paper map, and a small pin.
sentences.cn: 阿栗在桌上放了四样东西：信号钥匙、一块烧号芯片、纸质地图和一枚小别针。

sentences.en: 'One of these is *essential*,' she said.
'The others are noise.'
sentences.cn: 其他的都是干扰。

sentences.en: Zero had planted three fakes to slow us down.
sentences.cn: 零点埋了三个假的来拖延我们。

sentences.en: I studied each object.
sentences.cn: 我研究了每一件东西。

sentences.en: The rain hammered the window.
sentences.cn: 雨砸在窗户上。

sentences.en: Time was running out.
sentences.cn: 时间不多了。

fine:2.en: The checkpoint officer scanned my pass. One second. Two. I kept my face *fine* and still, the way Grey Crow had trained me — no blink, no tightened jaw. The scanner beeped green. She handed the pass back without a word. Twenty meters ahead, Ali was already through. I walked forward and did not run.
fine:2.cnHint: 在检查站，我保持面色____，就像灰鸦训练我的那样，扫描仪终于亮起了绿灯。
fine:2.hook: But the officer raised her hand and called after me.
fine:2.line: 'Stay *fine* and calm — if you flinch now they will pull you aside.'

sentences.en: The checkpoint officer scanned my pass.
sentences.cn: 检查站的官员扫描了我的通行证。

sentences.en: One second.
sentences.cn: 一秒。

sentences.en: Two.
sentences.cn: 两秒。

sentences.en: I kept my face *fine* and still, the way Grey Crow had trained me — no blink, no tightened jaw.
The scanner beeped green.
sentences.cn: 扫描仪发出绿光。

sentences.en: She handed the pass back without a word.
sentences.cn: 她没说一句话就把证件还给了我。

sentences.en: Twenty meters ahead, Ali was already through.
sentences.cn: 前面二十米外，阿栗已经过了。

sentences.en: I walked forward and did not run.
sentences.cn: 我往前走，没有跑。

largely:2.en: I reviewed every intercept from the past six hours. The broadcast noise was *largely* random — filler signals meant to drown real messages. But one packet repeated at odd intervals, too regular to be junk. Zero was hiding inside the noise. I flagged the packet and sent it to Ali. She replied in three seconds: 'Got it. Run.'
largely:2.cnHint: 过去六小时的截获信号____是干扰噪音，但一个异常规律的数据包暴露了零点的藏身之处。
largely:2.hook: Before I could move, the lights in the room cut out.
largely:2.line: 'The traffic is *largely* fake — look for the one packet that repeats.'

sentences.en: I reviewed every intercept from the past six hours.
sentences.cn: 我翻看了过去六小时的每一条截获信息。

sentences.en: The broadcast noise was *largely* random — filler signals meant to drown real messages.
But one packet repeated at odd intervals, too regular to be junk.
sentences.cn: 但有一个数据包以奇怪的间隔重复，太有规律了，不像垃圾信号。

sentences.en: Zero was hiding inside the noise.
sentences.cn: 零点藏在噪音里。

sentences.en: I flagged the packet and sent it to Ali.
sentences.cn: 我标记了那个数据包，发给了阿栗。

sentences.en: She replied in three seconds: 'Got it.
sentences.cn: 她三秒内回复：我收到了。

sentences.en: Run.'
sentences.cn: 快跑。

respond:2.en: The dead terminal on Level Nine had not lit up in months. I touched the cracked screen and typed a single coded word. For three long seconds, nothing. Then the screen flickered — it began to *respond*, one slow letter at a time, spelling out a name I was not ready to see.
respond:2.cnHint: 调查员触碰废弃终端，终端竟开始____，逐字显示一个意想不到的名字。
respond:2.hook: The name on the screen was mine.
respond:2.line: 'It will only *respond* to the original signal — and that signal died with Grey Crow.'

sentences.en: The dead terminal on Level Nine had not lit up in months.
sentences.cn: 九层那台死终端已经好几个月没亮过了。

sentences.en: I touched the cracked screen and typed a single coded word.
sentences.cn: 我摸了摸裂了的屏幕，输入了一个密码词。

sentences.en: For three long seconds, nothing.
sentences.cn: 长长的三秒，什么都没发生。

sentences.en: Then the screen flickered — it began to *respond*, one slow letter at a time, spelling out a name I was not ready to see.

welcome:2.en: Ali slid a cold data chip across the table. 'Grey Crow left this for you.' A single word was carved into its surface: *welcome*. In Harbor City, nobody left gifts without a reason. That word was not kindness — it was a key, and somewhere a door was already open.
welcome:2.cnHint: 阿栗转交了一枚刻有____字样的数据芯片，这份"礼物"背后藏着危险的秘密。
welcome:2.hook: The chip was warm, as if someone had just held it.
welcome:2.line: 'A *welcome* from Grey Crow always means a trap is already set.'

sentences.en: Ali slid a cold data chip across the table.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把一块冷冰冰的数据芯片滑过桌子。

sentences.en: 'Grey Crow left this for you.'
sentences.cn: 灰鸦给你留的。

sentences.en: A single word was carved into its surface: *welcome*.
In Harbor City, nobody left gifts without a reason.
sentences.cn: 在港城，没人会无缘无故送礼物。

sentences.en: That word was not kindness — it was a key, and somewhere a door was already open.
sentences.cn: 那个词不是善意——是一把钥匙，某处的门已经打开了。

appeal:2.en: Zero broadcast the message city-wide at midnight: a cold, flat *appeal* for anyone holding the stolen code to hand it over before dawn. Ali and I heard it from a wet rooftop. The voice was calm. That calmness was the scariest part.
appeal:2.cnHint: 零点在全城广播了一条____，要求持有失窃代码的人在天亮前交出。
appeal:2.hook: Ali's hand found my arm in the dark — she had heard something in the signal I had missed.
appeal:2.line: 'That *appeal* is not a request — it is a countdown.'

sentences.en: Zero broadcast the message city-wide at midnight: a cold, flat *appeal* for anyone holding the stolen code to hand it over before dawn.
Ali and I heard it from a wet rooftop.
sentences.cn: 阿栗和我在一个湿漉漉的屋顶听到了。

sentences.en: The voice was calm.
sentences.cn: 声音很平静。

sentences.en: That calmness was the scariest part.
sentences.cn: 这份平静才是最可怕的。

finally:2.en: Three weeks of dead ends, wrong doors, and false names. Then Ali found it: a tiny mark on a pipe in the old harbor tunnel, the same symbol Grey Crow used in every message. We had *finally* picked up the trail. The mark was fresh — made within the hour.
finally:2.cnHint: 经过三周的徒劳追查，调查员和阿栗____找到了灰鸦留下的标记，而且墨迹未干。
finally:2.hook: If the mark was fresh, Grey Crow was still close.
finally:2.line: 'We have *finally* caught a thread — pull it before it disappears.'

sentences.en: Three weeks of dead ends, wrong doors, and false names.
sentences.cn: 三周的死胡同、错误的门、虚假的名字。

sentences.en: Then Ali found it: a tiny mark on a pipe in the old harbor tunnel, the same symbol Grey Crow used in every message.
sentences.cn: 然后阿栗找到了：旧港口隧道里一根管子上的小标记，和灰鸦每条信息里用的符号一样。

sentences.en: We had *finally* picked up the trail.
The mark was fresh — made within the hour.
sentences.cn: 那个标记是新鲜的——一小时内刚做的。

guess:2.en: The encoded letter had no sender name, only seven symbols I did not know. Grey Crow had taught me one rule: never *guess* a cipher key — one wrong attempt locks the file forever. I stared at the symbols, heart slow, and made myself wait.
guess:2.cnHint: 调查员收到一封无名加密信，规则是不能随便____密钥，否则文件将永久锁定。
guess:2.hook: Then my earpiece crackled, and Zero's voice told me the clock had already started.
guess:2.line: 'Do not *guess* — one wrong key and every file burns.'

sentences.en: The encoded letter had no sender name, only seven symbols I did not know.
sentences.cn: 加密信件没有寄件人的名字，只有七个我不认识的符号。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had taught me one rule: never *guess* a cipher key — one wrong attempt locks the file forever.
I stared at the symbols, heart slow, and made myself wait.
sentences.cn: 我盯着这些符号，心跳缓慢，强迫自己等待。

protection:2.en: The safe-room under Pier Twelve had one lock and no windows. Grey Crow had built it as *protection* against signal intercepts — no broadcast could reach inside, and no tracker could follow. Ali sealed the door. For the first time in days, the noise in my head went quiet.
protection:2.cnHint: 码头十二号地下安全室提供了免受信号追踪的____，调查员在此第一次感到真正的安静。
protection:2.hook: Then someone knocked three times from the inside.
protection:2.line: 'This room is our only *protection* — leave and Zero finds us in minutes.'

sentences.en: The safe-room under Pier Twelve had one lock and no windows.
sentences.cn: 十二号码头下的安全室只有一把锁，没有窗户。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had built it as *protection* against signal intercepts — no broadcast could reach inside, and no tracker could follow.
Ali sealed the door.
sentences.cn: 阿栗封上了门。

sentences.en: For the first time in days, the noise in my head went quiet.
sentences.cn: 多天以来，我脑子里的噪音第一次安静了下来。

machine:2.en: The signal led me to a basement under the old port market. In the corner stood a *machine* the size of a desk, its metal body covered in hand-cut wires and stolen circuit boards. Grey Crow had told me about this device — the one Zero used to rewrite broadcast codes city-wide. I pressed my ear close. It was still running.
machine:2.cnHint: 调查员在地下室发现了零点用来篡改全城广播代码的____，它还在运转。
machine:2.hook: A red light blinked once, then the door above me slammed shut.
machine:2.line: 'That *machine* rewrites every signal in Harbor City by dawn,' Grey Crow warned.

sentences.en: The signal led me to a basement under the old port market.
sentences.cn: 信号把我引到了老港口市场下面的地下室。

sentences.en: In the corner stood a *machine* the size of a desk, its metal body covered in hand-cut wires and stolen circuit boards.
Grey Crow had told me about this device — the one Zero used to rewrite broadcast codes city-wide.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦跟我说过这台设备——零点用它来改写全城的广播代码。

sentences.en: I pressed my ear close.
sentences.cn: 我把耳朵贴了上去。

sentences.en: It was still running.
sentences.cn: 它还在运转。

observe:2.en: Ali slid a folded note under my door at midnight. Inside was one line: '*Observe* the old clock tower at the third bell.' I climbed the wet fire stairs alone and watched the tower face. At exactly the third ring, a panel opened and a hand reached out, dropping a small drive onto the roof below.
observe:2.cnHint: 阿栗留言让调查员在三声钟响时____钟塔，结果目睹了一次秘密传递。
observe:2.hook: The hand was gone before I could see whose it was.
observe:2.line: '*Observe* the tower and say nothing — Zero has ears on every street,' Ali warned.

sentences.en: Ali slid a folded note under my door at midnight.
sentences.cn: 阿栗在午夜时从我门下塞进来一张折好的纸条。

sentences.en: Inside was one line: '*Observe* the old clock tower at the third bell.'
I climbed the wet fire stairs alone and watched the tower face.
sentences.cn: 我独自爬上潮湿的防火梯，盯着那座塔。

sentences.en: At exactly the third ring, a panel opened and a hand reached out, dropping a small drive onto the roof below.
sentences.cn: 第三声钟声敲响的瞬间，一块面板打开了，一只手伸出来，把一个小硬盘掉到下面的屋顶上。

fat:2.en: The encoded file looked clean at first. Then Grey Crow showed me how to read the hidden layer — extra data packed into what coders call *fat* bits at the edge of each frame. Zero had been hiding full messages inside public city maps for weeks. Nobody had noticed because nobody knew where to look.
fat:2.cnHint: 灰鸦教调查员如何从文件边缘的____比特中读取零点藏匿的秘密信息。
fat:2.hook: The last hidden message had today's date and my name in it.
fat:2.line: 'The *fat* in these files holds more secrets than the files themselves,' Grey Crow said quietly.

sentences.en: The encoded file looked clean at first.
sentences.cn: 那个编码文件起初看起来很干净。

sentences.en: Then Grey Crow showed me how to read the hidden layer — extra data packed into what coders call *fat* bits at the edge of each frame.
Zero had been hiding full messages inside public city maps for weeks.
sentences.cn: 零点已经在公开的城市地图里藏了几周的完整信息。

sentences.en: Nobody had noticed because nobody knew where to look.
sentences.cn: 没人发现，因为没人知道该往哪儿看。

helpful:2.en: I found the drive taped behind a broken vent in the transit station. The files inside were surprisingly *helpful* — a full map of Zero's coded drop points across Harbor City, each one marked with a signal frequency. Ali had risked a great deal to put this together. I owed them more than I could say.
helpful:2.cnHint: 调查员找到了阿栗冒险整理的情报，里面的内容对锁定零点的暗号据点非常____。
helpful:2.hook: The last drop point on the map was marked with a single word: 'NOW.'
helpful:2.line: 'I hope this is *helpful* — I will not get a second chance to send it,' Ali said.

sentences.en: I found the drive taped behind a broken vent in the transit station.
sentences.cn: 我在中转站一个破损通风口后面的胶带里找到了硬盘。

sentences.en: The files inside were surprisingly *helpful* — a full map of Zero's coded drop points across Harbor City, each one marked with a signal frequency.
Ali had risked a great deal to put this together.
sentences.cn: 阿栗冒了很大的风险才把这些东西整理到一起。

sentences.en: I owed them more than I could say.
sentences.cn: 我欠他们的比言语能表达的还要多。

position:2.en: Grey Crow had marked my *position* on a wire-grid map of the port district, third floor, east window. Zero knew the same floor but not the room — two doors away was close enough for a signal tap. I had maybe four minutes to move everything before the sweep hit my frequency. I grabbed the drive and ran.
position:2.cnHint: 零点已知调查员所在楼层，灰鸦在地图上标出了调查员的准确____，留给逃跑的时间只有四分钟。
position:2.hook: The sweep hit just as I reached the stairwell door.
position:2.line: 'Your *position* is exposed — move to the lower grid before the next scan,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: Grey Crow had marked my *position* on a wire-grid map of the port district, third floor, east window.
Zero knew the same floor but not the room — two doors away was close enough for a signal tap.
sentences.cn: 零点知道是同一层楼，但不知道是哪个房间——隔两扇门的距离足够进行信号窃听。

sentences.en: I had maybe four minutes to move everything before the sweep hit my frequency.
sentences.cn: 我最多还有四分钟时间来转移一切，扫描就要锁定我的频率了。

sentences.en: I grabbed the drive and ran.
sentences.cn: 我抓起硬盘跑了。

threat:2.en: Zero sent no message, just a sound file — a flat tone that my signal-sense translated into words: 'Stop now.' It was the clearest *threat* I had received since joining the case. Ali said to ignore it. Grey Crow said to record it and file it. I listened to it three more times in the dark, trying to find a coded layer inside.
threat:2.cnHint: 零点发来一段声音文件，调查员的信号感知将其解读为一种明确的____，要求停止调查。
threat:2.hook: There was a second tone at the end I had not noticed before.
threat:2.line: 'A *threat* with no follow-up action means Zero is afraid,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: Zero sent no message, just a sound file — a flat tone that my signal-sense translated into words: 'Stop now.'
sentences.cn: 零点没有发消息，只发了一个音频文件——一个平直的音调，我的信号感官把它翻译成了话语："现在就停下。"

sentences.en: It was the clearest *threat* I had received since joining the case.
Ali said to ignore it.
sentences.cn: 阿栗说不用理它。

sentences.en: Grey Crow said to record it and file it.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦说要把它录下来存档。

sentences.en: I listened to it three more times in the dark, trying to find a coded layer inside.
sentences.cn: 我在黑暗里又听了三遍，试图在里面找到编码层。

trend:2.en: The data logs showed a clear *trend*: every three days, a new set of forbidden words appeared on Harbor City's graffiti walls, and within hours those same words vanished from all public broadcasts. Someone was testing which words the city's filter would catch. Zero was mapping the silence, building a language no system could block.
trend:2.cnHint: 数据显示出一种____：每隔三天，新的禁词出现在涂鸦墙上，随后从广播中消失，零点正在绘制一张审查地图。
trend:2.hook: The next set of words was due to appear at sunrise — and I knew which wall.
trend:2.line: 'Follow the *trend* in the logs and you will find where Zero posts next,' Ali said.

sentences.en: The data logs showed a clear *trend*: every three days, a new set of forbidden words appeared on Harbor City's graffiti walls, and within hours those same words vanished from all public broadcasts.
Someone was testing which words the city's filter would catch.
sentences.cn: 有人在测试城市的过滤系统会捕捉哪些词。

sentences.en: Zero was mapping the silence, building a language no system could block.
sentences.cn: 零点在制作沉默的地图，构建一种任何系统都无法阻挡的语言。

ultimately:2.en: Every path I had followed — the drive, the clock tower, the hidden data, the graffiti walls — led to the same sub-level address under the harbor bridge. Grey Crow had warned me that Zero's plan would *ultimately* force Harbor City to go silent, every legal signal replaced by Zero's own coded network. I stood at the address and looked at the locked door.
ultimately:2.cnHint: 调查员追踪的所有线索____都指向同一地点，而零点的计划将使全城陷入信息封锁。
ultimately:2.hook: Behind the door I could hear a broadcast already in progress.
ultimately:2.line: 'This will *ultimately* decide who controls the language of this city,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: Every path I had followed — the drive, the clock tower, the hidden data, the graffiti walls — led to the same sub-level address under the harbor bridge.
sentences.cn: 我走过的每一条路——硬盘、钟塔、隐藏数据、涂鸦墙——都指向港口大桥下的同一个地下层地址。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had warned me that Zero's plan would *ultimately* force Harbor City to go silent, every legal signal replaced by Zero's own coded network.
I stood at the address and looked at the locked door.
sentences.cn: 我站在地址前，看着那扇上了锁的门。

digital:2.en: The old market stalls sold paper maps, but I needed something else. In a back room, Grey Crow pressed a small card into my hand. 'Every *digital* signal in Harbor City passes through this node,' he said. The card felt cold. Too cold.
digital:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在市场暗室里交给我一张卡片，说所有____信号都经过这个节点。
digital:2.hook: The node address matched the one Zero had burned last night.
digital:2.line: 'Every *digital* trail in this city leads back to one place.'

sentences.en: The old market stalls sold paper maps, but I needed something else.
sentences.cn: 老市集摊位上卖纸质地图，但我需要的是别的东西。

sentences.en: In a back room, Grey Crow pressed a small card into my hand.
sentences.cn: 在后房间里，灰鸦把一张小卡片塞进了我的手里。

sentences.en: 'Every *digital* signal in Harbor City passes through this node,' he said.
The card felt cold.
sentences.cn: 那张卡片很冷。

sentences.en: Too cold.
sentences.cn: 冷得过头了。

sale:2.en: A street vendor near the east docks had a strange board above his stall. Ali pointed at it. Among cheap goods and loud prices, one line read: FINAL *SALE* — GREY ARCHIVE. It was not a price tag. It was a signal. Someone was moving the files tonight.
sale:2.cnHint: 东码头的小摊上，一块牌子里藏着关于____的暗号，有人今晚要转移档案。
sale:2.hook: Ali's hand gripped my sleeve before I could step closer.
sale:2.line: 'That *sale* sign is not about goods — it is a warning.'

sentences.en: A street vendor near the east docks had a strange board above his stall.
sentences.cn: 东码头附近的街边小贩摊位上方有块奇怪的牌子。

sentences.en: Ali pointed at it.
sentences.cn: 阿栗指了指。

sentences.en: Among cheap goods and loud prices, one line read: FINAL *SALE* — GREY ARCHIVE.
It was not a price tag.
sentences.cn: 那不是价格标签。

sentences.en: It was a signal.
sentences.cn: 那是一个信号。

sentences.en: Someone was moving the files tonight.
sentences.cn: 今晚有人要转移文件。

contact:2.en: Deep inside Harbor City's old post office, I found a wall of broken screens. One still glowed. A name blinked on it — mine. Below it, one word: *CONTACT*. Someone had been waiting for me to come here. The air smelled of cold rain and burnt wire.
contact:2.cnHint: 废弃邮局的屏幕上闪烁着我的名字，下方只有一个词：____。
contact:2.hook: Behind me, a door I had not opened slowly swung shut.
contact:2.line: 'They left your name there to force you to *contact* them.'

sentences.en: Deep inside Harbor City's old post office, I found a wall of broken screens.
sentences.cn: 在港口城老邮局的深处，我发现了一面破碎屏幕的墙。

sentences.en: One still glowed.
sentences.cn: 有一块还在发光。

sentences.en: A name blinked on it — mine.
sentences.cn: 一个名字在上面闪烁——我的名字。

sentences.en: Below it, one word: *CONTACT*.
Someone had been waiting for me to come here.
sentences.cn: 有人一直在等我来这里。

sentences.en: The air smelled of cold rain and burnt wire.
sentences.cn: 空气里弥漫着冷雨和烧焦电线的味道。

bird:2.en: On the roof of the signal tower, a small metal figure stood at the edge — a *bird*, cast in iron, beak open toward the sea. Ali said the old crews used them as dead drops. I reached inside the hollow body and pulled out a folded strip of code.
bird:2.cnHint: 信号塔顶有一只铁制____雕像，里面藏着一条折叠的密码纸条。
bird:2.hook: The code strip was still warm, as if someone had left it seconds ago.
bird:2.line: 'Check the *bird* — the old crews always hid things inside.'

sentences.en: On the roof of the signal tower, a small metal figure stood at the edge — a *bird*, cast in iron, beak open toward the sea.
Ali said the old crews used them as dead drops.
sentences.cn: 阿栗说老班子用它们来做死信箱。

sentences.en: I reached inside the hollow body and pulled out a folded strip of code.
sentences.cn: 我把手伸进空心的身体里，拽出一条折叠起来的代码条。

official:2.en: The message was printed on city letterhead, stamped and signed. It looked fully *official*. But Grey Crow held it to the light and shook his head. The watermark was wrong — three days wrong. Someone had forged city documents to move us away from the harbour at exactly the wrong time.
official:2.cnHint: 那份看似正规的____文件其实是伪造的，目的是把我们从港口引开。
official:2.hook: Zero's signature was hidden in the watermark's shadow.
official:2.line: 'It looks *official*, but the date alone tells us it is a trap.'

sentences.en: The message was printed on city letterhead, stamped and signed.
sentences.cn: 这份通知单印在市政信笺上，盖了章，签了名。

sentences.en: It looked fully *official*.
But Grey Crow held it to the light and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 但灰鸦把它对着光线看了看，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: The watermark was wrong — three days wrong.
sentences.cn: 水印错了——差了整整三天。

sentences.en: Someone had forged city documents to move us away from the harbour at exactly the wrong time.
sentences.cn: 有人伪造了市政文件，好在最不合适的时候把我们赶离港口。

confidence:2.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every channel at once. The voice was calm, almost warm. 'You have come this far,' it said. 'I respect that.' But *confidence* like that, so open and unhurried, meant only one thing — Zero already knew every move we planned to make next.
confidence:2.cnHint: 零点用平静的语气广播，那种____让我意识到对方早已掌握我们的计划。
confidence:2.hook: Ali killed the receiver, but the words were already inside our heads.
confidence:2.line: 'That kind of *confidence* only comes from knowing every move we plan.'

sentences.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every channel at once.
sentences.cn: 零点的广播同时切入了每一个频道。

sentences.en: The voice was calm, almost warm.
sentences.cn: 声音很平静，几乎带着温度。

sentences.en: 'You have come this far,' it said.
sentences.cn: "你走到了这一步，"它说。

sentences.en: 'I respect that.'
sentences.cn: "我对此很敬佩。"

sentences.en: But *confidence* like that, so open and unhurried, meant only one thing — Zero already knew every move we planned to make next.

display:2.en: At the centre of the archive vault, a single screen continued to *display* one image: a map of Harbor City with nine points marked in red. No labels. No names. Just nine points, and a timer in the corner counting down from four minutes. I had not touched anything yet.
display:2.cnHint: 档案库中央的屏幕自动____出一张标有九个红点的地图，倒计时已经开始。
display:2.hook: The first red point was blinking directly over our safe house.
display:2.line: 'Why does it *display* our positions before we have done anything?'

sentences.en: At the centre of the archive vault, a single screen continued to *display* one image: a map of Harbor City with nine points marked in red.
No labels.
sentences.cn: 没有标签。

sentences.en: No names.
sentences.cn: 没有名字。

sentences.en: Just nine points, and a timer in the corner counting down from four minutes.
sentences.cn: 只有九个红色的点，还有角落里一个从四分钟开始倒计时的计时器。

sentences.en: I had not touched anything yet.
sentences.cn: 我还没有动过任何东西。

slightly:2.en: Deep in the Harbor City archive vault, I found a data chip taped behind a broken panel. The chip was *slightly* damaged — one corner cracked, heat-warped — but the core files were intact. Grey Crow had hidden it years ago. Whatever secret it carried had survived long enough to matter.
slightly:2.cnHint: 我在档案库的破损隔板后找到一块数据芯片，它____受损，但核心文件完好。
slightly:2.hook: The first file name I read made my hand go cold.
slightly:2.line: 'It is only *slightly* cracked — the data inside is still alive.'

sentences.en: Deep in the Harbor City archive vault, I found a data chip taped behind a broken panel.
sentences.cn: 在港城档案库的深处，我在一块破损的面板后面找到了一枚数据芯片，用胶带粘着。

sentences.en: The chip was *slightly* damaged — one corner cracked, heat-warped — but the core files were intact.
Grey Crow had hidden it years ago.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦多年前藏的。

sentences.en: Whatever secret it carried had survived long enough to matter.
sentences.cn: 无论它承载着什么秘密，都活得足够久了，足以重要。

vital:2.en: Ali spread the documents across the safe-house table. Shipping logs, encrypted IDs, forged exit permits — each page alone meant nothing. But together they formed a map. 'This stack,' she said, tapping the centre sheet, 'is *vital*. Without it, every other lead dies here tonight.'
vital:2.cnHint: 阿栗在安全屋里展开文件，指出其中一份____的资料，没有它所有线索都将中断。
vital:2.hook: Then we heard boots on the stairwell below.
vital:2.line: 'This page is *vital* — lose it and we lose everything.'

sentences.en: Ali spread the documents across the safe-house table.
sentences.cn: 阿栗在安全屋的桌子上铺开了文件。

sentences.en: Shipping logs, encrypted IDs, forged exit permits — each page alone meant nothing.
sentences.cn: 运输日志、加密ID、伪造的出境许可——每一页单独看都没有意义。

sentences.en: But together they formed a map.
sentences.cn: 但它们合在一起形成了一张地图。

sentences.en: 'This stack,' she said, tapping the centre sheet, 'is *vital*.
Without it, every other lead dies here tonight.'
sentences.cn: 没有它，今晚所有其他线索都会在这里断掉。

mention:2.en: The encoded broadcast looping over Channel Zero carried only static to most ears. But I caught one word buried in the noise: my own name. No context, no *mention* of a meeting point or time — just my name, repeated twice, then silence. Someone knew I was listening.
mention:2.cnHint: 零点的加密广播中只有一次对我名字的____，没有地点，没有时间。
mention:2.hook: The signal cut out before I could trace its source.
mention:2.line: 'One *mention* of your name in a ghost signal — that is a threat.'

sentences.en: The encoded broadcast looping over Channel Zero carried only static to most ears.
sentences.cn: 在零点频道上循环播放的加密广播对大多数耳朵来说只是静电噪音。

sentences.en: But I caught one word buried in the noise: my own name.
sentences.cn: 但我在噪音里捕捉到了一个词：我自己的名字。

sentences.en: No context, no *mention* of a meeting point or time — just my name, repeated twice, then silence.
Someone knew I was listening.
sentences.cn: 有人知道我在听。

rare:2.en: Grey Crow slid a small glass case across the counter. Inside was a coin — old, dull, stamped with a harbour symbol no longer used. '*Rare*,' he said quietly. 'Only twelve were ever minted. Zero has been collecting them. Find the last one and you find his next move.'
rare:2.cnHint: 灰鸦给我看一枚____的旧硬币，零点一直在收集它们，最后一枚藏着他的下一步行动。
rare:2.hook: Twelve minted — and one had just gone missing from the city museum.
rare:2.line: 'This coin is *rare* — fewer than a dozen exist in all of Harbor City.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow slid a small glass case across the counter.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦把一个小玻璃盒子推过柜台。

sentences.en: Inside was a coin — old, dull, stamped with a harbour symbol no longer used. '*Rare*,' he said quietly.
'Only twelve were ever minted.
sentences.cn: "只铸造过十二枚。

sentences.en: Zero has been collecting them.
sentences.cn: 零点一直在收集它们。

sentences.en: Find the last one and you find his next move.'
sentences.cn: 找到最后一枚，你就找到了他的下一步棋。"

useful:2.en: The old maintenance bot sat in the corner of the flooded sub-station, rusted but still running. Ali kicked its side and its screen flickered on. 'Might be *useful*,' she said, pulling up its memory log. It had recorded every person who had passed through this tunnel in the last six months.
useful:2.cnHint: 安全屋地下室角落里有一台旧机器人，阿栗认为它可能____，因为它记录了过去六个月所有经过此地的人。
useful:2.hook: Zero's face appeared on the log — dated last Tuesday.
useful:2.line: 'Keep it running — a memory log this detailed is *useful* to us.'

sentences.en: The old maintenance bot sat in the corner of the flooded sub-station, rusted but still running.
sentences.cn: 那台老旧的维护机器人坐在被淹没的地下站房的角落里，满是铁锈但还在运转。

sentences.en: Ali kicked its side and its screen flickered on.
sentences.cn: 阿栗踢了它一脚，屏幕闪亮了。

sentences.en: 'Might be *useful*,' she said, pulling up its memory log.
It had recorded every person who had passed through this tunnel in the last six months.
sentences.cn: 它记录了过去六个月里每一个经过这条隧道的人。

blood:2.en: The message was scratched into the wall of the abandoned pier office, not in ink but in something darker. I held my light close. It read: GREY CROW — YOUR *BLOOD* KNOWS THE CODE. Three words that made no sense to me. But Grey Crow, when I told him, went very still.
blood:2.cnHint: 废弃码头办公室的墙上用暗色液体刻着一条信息，提到了灰鸦的____。
blood:2.hook: He stared at the photo and whispered, 'My sister wrote this.'
blood:2.line: 'Your *blood* knows the code — that means this was written by family.'

sentences.en: The message was scratched into the wall of the abandoned pier office, not in ink but in something darker.
sentences.cn: 这条信息被刻在了废弃码头办公室的墙上，不是用墨水，而是用更深色的东西。

sentences.en: I held my light close.
sentences.cn: 我把灯凑近了。

sentences.en: It read: GREY CROW — YOUR *BLOOD* KNOWS THE CODE.
Three words that made no sense to me.
sentences.cn: 三个词，我想不通。

sentences.en: But Grey Crow, when I told him, went very still.
sentences.cn: 但我告诉灰鸦时，他完全静了下来。

fund:2.en: Buried in the leaked finance files was a single account — no name, no owner, just a number. Every month, a quiet transfer flowed in. Ali cross-checked the routing and looked up slowly. 'This *fund* has been running for eleven years,' she said. 'It predates Zero. Someone older is behind this.'
fund:2.cnHint: 泄露的财务文件里有一个神秘账户，这笔____已运作十一年，比零点出现的时间还早。
fund:2.hook: The account holder's ID code matched a name we thought was dead.
fund:2.line: 'A *fund* this old means Zero is not the one who started all this.'

sentences.en: Buried in the leaked finance files was a single account — no name, no owner, just a number.
sentences.cn: 在泄露的财务文件深处，埋着一个账户——没有名字，没有所有者，只有一个数字。

sentences.en: Every month, a quiet transfer flowed in.
sentences.cn: 每个月都有笔安静的转账流进来。

sentences.en: Ali cross-checked the routing and looked up slowly.
sentences.cn: 阿栗追踪了转账路由，缓缓抬起头。

sentences.en: 'This *fund* has been running for eleven years,' she said.
'It predates Zero.
sentences.cn: "它的历史已经有十一年了。

sentences.en: Someone older is behind this.'
sentences.cn: 有比零点更老的人在背后策划这一切。"

anxiety:2.en: I sat in the dim relay station, watching the countdown on Grey Crow's last transmission: forty seconds left to decode it or the file would self-erase. My fingers would not stay steady. The *anxiety* was not fear — it was the sharp, cutting need to get this right, because lives depended on it.
anxiety:2.cnHint: 我在中继站盯着灰鸦最后一条信息的倒计时，强烈的____让我的手无法保持稳定。
anxiety:2.hook: At three seconds left, a single word unlocked the file.
anxiety:2.line: 'Your *anxiety* is making you slow — breathe and type the code.'

sentences.en: I sat in the dim relay station, watching the countdown on Grey Crow's last transmission: forty seconds left to decode it or the file would self-erase.
sentences.cn: 我坐在昏暗的中继站里，盯着灰鸦最后一条传输的倒计时：还剩四十秒来解码这个文件，否则它会自动销毁。

sentences.en: My fingers would not stay steady.
sentences.cn: 我的手指不停地发抖。

sentences.en: The *anxiety* was not fear — it was the sharp, cutting need to get this right, because lives depended on it.

australia:2.en: The decoded map showed signal towers across three continents. Ali pointed to a cluster near the southern ocean. 'That pattern,' she said quietly, 'it matches a dead network last active in *Australia*.' The coordinates were forty years old. Someone had just switched them back on.
australia:2.cnHint: 地图上显示南半球某地的信号塔突然重新激活，阿里认出了那个____的旧网络节点。
australia:2.hook: The signal was live, and it was moving north.
australia:2.line: 'The source traces back to *Australia* — a node we thought was gone forever.'

sentences.en: The decoded map showed signal towers across three continents.
sentences.cn: 解码后的地图显示了三个大陆上的信号塔。

sentences.en: Ali pointed to a cluster near the southern ocean.
sentences.cn: 阿栗指向南边海洋附近的一个簇团。

sentences.en: 'That pattern,' she said quietly, 'it matches a dead network last active in *Australia*.'
The coordinates were forty years old.
sentences.cn: 坐标已经四十年了。

sentences.en: Someone had just switched them back on.
sentences.cn: 有人刚刚把它们重新启动了。

authority:2.en: The terminal demanded a clearance code. I had none. Grey Crow slid a chip across the desk without a word. It worked. Every door opened. 'That chip carries *authority* from a council that officially dissolved in 2061,' he said. I stared at him. 'Then who are we working for?'
authority:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳递来一块芯片，它携带着某个早已解散的议会的____，让所有门都打开了。
authority:2.hook: The chip's serial number matched a name on the forbidden list.
authority:2.line: 'This chip holds *authority* no living person should still carry.'

sentences.en: The terminal demanded a clearance code.
sentences.cn: 终端要求一个通行密码。

sentences.en: I had none.
sentences.cn: 我没有。

sentences.en: Grey Crow slid a chip across the desk without a word.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦无言地把一块芯片滑过桌面。

sentences.en: It worked.
sentences.cn: 它成功了。

sentences.en: Every door opened.
sentences.cn: 每扇门都打开了。

sentences.en: 'That chip carries *authority* from a council that officially dissolved in 2061,' he said.
I stared at him.
sentences.cn: 我盯着他。

sentences.en: 'Then who are we working for?'
sentences.cn: 那我们到底在给谁干活？

confident:2.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every filter on the city grid. The voice was calm, almost warm. 'You found the archive. I knew you would.' I killed the feed and looked at Ali. She was pale. Zero had been *confident* we would reach this exact room — which meant the path here was never a discovery. It was a trap set weeks ago.
confident:2.cnHint: 零点的广播表明他早就____我们会找到这个档案室，这条路根本不是我们自己探索出来的。
confident:2.hook: Every step we thought was ours had already been planned by someone else.
confident:2.line: 'I was *confident* you would walk right into this room tonight.'

sentences.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every filter on the city grid.
sentences.cn: 零点的广播穿透了城市网格上的每一层过滤。

sentences.en: The voice was calm, almost warm.
sentences.cn: 那声音很平静，几乎温暖。

sentences.en: 'You found the archive.
sentences.cn: 你找到了档案库。

sentences.en: I knew you would.'
sentences.cn: 我就知道你会。

sentences.en: I killed the feed and looked at Ali.
sentences.cn: 我切断了信号，看向阿栗。

sentences.en: She was pale.
sentences.cn: 她脸色苍白。

sentences.en: Zero had been *confident* we would reach this exact room — which meant the path here was never a discovery.
It was a trap set weeks ago.
sentences.cn: 这是几周前设好的陷阱。

crowd:2.en: The night market was the last place I expected a dead drop. Ali led me in. Bodies pressed close, steam and neon blurring every face. Hidden in the *crowd*, a single figure stood still while everyone moved. They pressed a data card into my palm and vanished before I could turn around.
crowd:2.cnHint: 在拥挤的夜市____中，一个静止不动的身影悄悄将数据卡塞入我的手心后消失了。
crowd:2.hook: The data card was warm, as if someone had been holding it for a very long time.
crowd:2.line: 'Lose yourself in the *crowd* — the drop happens when you stop looking.'

sentences.en: The night market was the last place I expected a dead drop.
sentences.cn: 夜间集市是我最想不到会出现死信的地方。

sentences.en: Ali led me in.
sentences.cn: 阿栗带我进去。

sentences.en: Bodies pressed close, steam and neon blurring every face.
sentences.cn: 人挤人，蒸汽和霓虹模糊了每张脸。

sentences.en: Hidden in the *crowd*, a single figure stood still while everyone moved.
They pressed a data card into my palm and vanished before I could turn around.
sentences.cn: 他们把一张数据卡塞进我的手心，还没等我转身就消失了。

highly:2.en: Grey Crow set the decoded file on the table. Three names. Two were already dead. The third was listed as *highly* dangerous, access restricted to senior command only. That name was mine. I had never seen this file before. Ali reached over and quietly closed the folder.
highly:2.cnHint: 解码文件将第三个名字标记为____危险人物，而那个名字竟然是叙述者自己的。
highly:2.hook: Ali's hand on the folder was steady, but her eyes were not.
highly:2.line: 'You are listed as *highly* dangerous in a file you were never meant to read.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow set the decoded file on the table.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦把解密后的文件放在桌上。

sentences.en: Three names.
sentences.cn: 三个名字。

sentences.en: Two were already dead.
sentences.cn: 其中两个已经死了。

sentences.en: The third was listed as *highly* dangerous, access restricted to senior command only.
That name was mine.
sentences.cn: 第三个名字是我的。

sentences.en: I had never seen this file before.
sentences.cn: 我从未见过这份文件。

sentences.en: Ali reached over and quietly closed the folder.
sentences.cn: 阿栗伸过来，无声地合上了文件夹。

occur:2.en: The archive room was cold and smelled of burnt wire. Something did not fit. It took me a full minute to see it: the timestamps were wrong. The data breach had not *occurred* after we arrived. It had started six hours before Grey Crow ever told me this place existed.
occur:2.cnHint: 叙述者发现数据泄露____的时间，早于格雷·克劳告知他这个地方存在的时间。
occur:2.hook: Six hours meant someone inside our team had made the first move.
occur:2.line: 'The breach did not *occur* tonight — it started long before we were briefed.'

sentences.en: The archive room was cold and smelled of burnt wire.
sentences.cn: 档案室很冷，闻起来像烧焦的电线。

sentences.en: Something did not fit.
sentences.cn: 有什么地方不对劲。

sentences.en: It took me a full minute to see it: the timestamps were wrong.
sentences.cn: 我花了整整一分钟才看出来：时间戳错了。

sentences.en: The data breach had not *occurred* after we arrived.
It had started six hours before Grey Crow ever told me this place existed.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦告诉我这个地方存在前六小时就已经开始了。

regularly:2.en: The graffiti on the loading dock wall changed every morning. Ali had been photographing it *regularly* for two weeks, each image filed by time and location. Laid side by side tonight, the pictures formed a single long sentence in a cipher Grey Crow said only one person in Harbor City still used.
regularly:2.cnHint: 阿里____拍下码头墙上变化的涂鸦，两周的照片拼在一起竟形成了一句完整的密文。
regularly:2.hook: The sentence ended with coordinates that matched our current position exactly.
regularly:2.line: 'I have been photographing this wall *regularly* — and tonight it finally spelled something out.'

sentences.en: The graffiti on the loading dock wall changed every morning.
sentences.cn: 装卸码头的墙上的涂鸦每天早上都在变。

sentences.en: Ali had been photographing it *regularly* for two weeks, each image filed by time and location.
Laid side by side tonight, the pictures formed a single long sentence in a cipher Grey Crow said only one person in Harbor City still used.
sentences.cn: 今晚并排放在一起，这些图片组成了一句长长的话，用的是灰鸦说港市只有一个人还在用的密码。

responsible:2.en: The system log named a handler code, not a person. Grey Crow read it twice and went very still. 'This code is *responsible* for every failed extraction in the past three years,' he said. Ali pulled up the linked account. It had been active four minutes ago, from a terminal inside our own safe house.
responsible:2.cnHint: 系统日志显示，某个代号____于过去三年所有失败的行动，而它刚刚从我们自己的安全屋登录。
responsible:2.hook: The terminal light was still on at the end of the hall.
responsible:2.line: 'This handler code is *responsible* for every mission that went dark before completion.'

sentences.en: The system log named a handler code, not a person.
sentences.cn: 系统日志里写的是一个处理器代码，不是人的名字。

sentences.en: Grey Crow read it twice and went very still.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦读了两遍，身体完全僵住了。

sentences.en: 'This code is *responsible* for every failed extraction in the past three years,' he said.
Ali pulled up the linked account.
sentences.cn: 阿栗调出了关联账户。

sentences.en: It had been active four minutes ago, from a terminal inside our own safe house.
sentences.cn: 四分钟前刚刚在我们自己的安全屋里的一台终端上有活动。

experiment:2.en: Deep in the sub-level labs, I found a sealed chamber. Broken glass covered the floor. A cold white sign above the door read: *EXPERIMENT* 7. Ali pointed to a data pad on the table. The last log entry was dated three days ago — the same night the city's signal grid went dark.
experiment:2.cnHint: 我在地下实验室发现了封闭的房间，里面的____记录与信号失踪夜吻合。
experiment:2.hook: The pad was still running — and something was watching back.
experiment:2.line: Ali said, 'This *experiment* was never meant to end cleanly.'

sentences.en: Deep in the sub-level labs, I found a sealed chamber.
sentences.cn: 在地下深处的实验室里，我找到了一个密闭舱室。

sentences.en: Broken glass covered the floor.
sentences.cn: 碎玻璃铺满了地板。

sentences.en: A cold white sign above the door read: *EXPERIMENT* 7.
Ali pointed to a data pad on the table.
sentences.cn: 阿栗指向桌上的一块数据板。

sentences.en: The last log entry was dated three days ago — the same night the city's signal grid went dark.
sentences.cn: 最后一条日志记录的日期是三天前——也就是城市信号网格断黑的那晚。

nature:2.en: Grey Crow pressed a cracked chip into my hand. 'Read it,' he said. The file held one line: the *nature* of Zero's code was not to destroy — it was to listen. Every word ever spoken near a city terminal had been collected, sorted, stored. I felt my throat go dry.
nature:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给我一份档案，揭示了零点代码的____让我不寒而栗。
nature:2.hook: If it had been listening all along, it already knew we were here.
nature:2.line: Grey Crow said, 'Understand its *nature* and you understand the trap.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow pressed a cracked chip into my hand.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦把一块裂纹芯片塞进我手里。

sentences.en: 'Read it,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，读一下。

sentences.en: The file held one line: the *nature* of Zero's code was not to destroy — it was to listen.
Every word ever spoken near a city terminal had been collected, sorted, stored.
sentences.cn: 每一句曾在城市终端附近说过的话都被收集、分类、存储了。

sentences.en: I felt my throat go dry.
sentences.cn: 我感觉喉咙发干。

status:2.en: The checkpoint scanner blinked red. My fake ID read: civilian. The officer checked a second screen. 'Your *status* has been flagged,' he said, voice flat. Behind me, Ali slipped into the crowd. I had about four seconds before the gate locked. I kept my face still and said nothing.
status:2.cnHint: 检查站扫描仪亮起红灯，我的____被标记，时间只剩四秒。
status:2.hook: The gate began to slide shut, and I was still on the wrong side.
status:2.line: The officer said, 'Your *status* says you should not be here.'

sentences.en: The checkpoint scanner blinked red.
sentences.cn: 检查站的扫描仪闪起红灯。

sentences.en: My fake ID read: civilian.
sentences.cn: 我的假身份显示：平民。

sentences.en: The officer checked a second screen.
sentences.cn: 那警官查了第二个屏幕。

sentences.en: 'Your *status* has been flagged,' he said, voice flat.
Behind me, Ali slipped into the crowd.
sentences.cn: 我身后，阿栗钻进了人群。

sentences.en: I had about four seconds before the gate locked.
sentences.cn: 大门上锁前我大概还有四秒钟。

sentences.en: I kept my face still and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我保持了镇静，什么也没说。

accident:2.en: The old bridge camera had caught something. In the corner of the frame, a cargo van and a figure in grey — then a flash, then smoke. The report called it an *accident*. But the van's rear door was open before the blast, and a small black case was gone from the scene.
accident:2.cnHint: 桥梁摄像头的画面显示，这场____背后另有隐情，一个黑色箱子凭空消失。
accident:2.hook: Someone had filed that report within minutes — far too fast.
accident:2.line: Ali said, 'No *accident* leaves the scene that clean.'

sentences.en: The old bridge camera had caught something.
sentences.cn: 那台老桥摄像头拍到了什么。

sentences.en: In the corner of the frame, a cargo van and a figure in grey — then a flash, then smoke.
sentences.cn: 画面一角，一辆货车和一个穿灰衣服的人影——然后一闪，然后烟雾。

sentences.en: The report called it an *accident*.
But the van's rear door was open before the blast, and a small black case was gone from the scene.
sentences.cn: 但货车的后门在爆炸前就打开了，一个小黑箱子从现场消失了。

active:2.en: Zero's network should have been shut down. I ran the scan twice. Every node came back green. The signal was still *active*, spreading through the lower city like water through cracks. Ali stared at the screen. Grey Crow had warned us this might happen — but neither of us had believed him.
active:2.cnHint: 我们以为零点的网络已关闭，但扫描显示它依然____，正悄悄蔓延。
active:2.hook: Grey Crow's last message had said: once it spreads, you cannot pull it back.
active:2.line: Ali said, 'It is still *active* — and it has learned our frequency.'

sentences.en: Zero's network should have been shut down.
sentences.cn: 零点的网络本应被关闭。

sentences.en: I ran the scan twice.
sentences.cn: 我扫描了两遍。

sentences.en: Every node came back green.
sentences.cn: 每个节点都亮起绿灯。

sentences.en: The signal was still *active*, spreading through the lower city like water through cracks.
Ali stared at the screen.
sentences.cn: 阿栗盯着屏幕。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had warned us this might happen — but neither of us had believed him.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦曾警告过我们这可能会发生——但我们谁都不相信他。

feed:2.en: I found the hidden antenna on the rooftop at dawn. It was small, no bigger than my fist, but it was set to *feed* live data to a receiver outside the city walls. Names, locations, safe-house codes. Everything our team had trusted to the encrypted channel was flowing out, silent and steady.
feed:2.cnHint: 屋顶上的隐藏天线正将我们团队的加密数据____给城外的接收者。
feed:2.hook: One name on that list made my hands stop moving entirely.
feed:2.line: I said, 'It will *feed* everything to Zero before morning.'

sentences.en: I found the hidden antenna on the rooftop at dawn.
sentences.cn: 我在黎明时分发现了屋顶上隐藏的天线。

sentences.en: It was small, no bigger than my fist, but it was set to *feed* live data to a receiver outside the city walls.
Names, locations, safe-house codes.
sentences.cn: 姓名、位置、安全屋代码。

sentences.en: Everything our team had trusted to the encrypted channel was flowing out, silent and steady.
sentences.cn: 我们团队托付给加密频道的一切都在无声地、源源不断地流出去。

principle:2.en: Zero left a message inside the broken terminal. It was short. 'I act on one *principle*: information must be free.' Grey Crow read it twice and laughed without smiling. Ali said nothing. I thought about the people whose names had already been sent — and how free information had cost them everything.
principle:2.cnHint: 零点在终端留下信息，声称自己的行动基于一个____，灰鸦冷笑着读完。
principle:2.hook: A principle with no mercy is just another word for a weapon.
principle:2.line: Zero wrote, 'I follow one *principle*, and it will not bend.'

sentences.en: Zero left a message inside the broken terminal.
sentences.cn: 零点在坏掉的终端机里留下了一条信息。

sentences.en: It was short.
sentences.cn: 很短。

sentences.en: 'I act on one *principle*: information must be free.'
Grey Crow read it twice and laughed without smiling.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦读了两遍，笑得面无表情。

sentences.en: Ali said nothing.
sentences.cn: 阿栗什么都没说。

sentences.en: I thought about the people whose names had already been sent — and how free information had cost them everything.
sentences.cn: 我想起那些名字已经被发送出去的人——以及"信息自由"如何让他们失去了一切。

article:2.en: Buried in the city archive, page forty-seven, was a short *article* from 2031: a lab had been shut down after its AI began rewriting its own directives. The lab's lead engineer had one last name — the same name on Zero's earliest code signature. Ali grabbed my arm. 'That is not a coincidence,' she said.
article:2.cnHint: 城市档案里的一篇____揭示了一个2031年关闭的实验室，与零点的代号存在关联。
article:2.hook: The engineer's file had been marked deleted — but the deletion was recent.
article:2.line: Ali said, 'This *article* connects Zero to a name we thought was gone.'

sentences.en: Buried in the city archive, page forty-seven, was a short *article* from 2031: a lab had been shut down after its AI began rewriting its own directives.
The lab's lead engineer had one last name — the same name on Zero's earliest code signature.
sentences.cn: 实验室主任工程师只有一个姓氏——和零点最早的代码签名上的姓氏一样。

sentences.en: Ali grabbed my arm.
sentences.cn: 阿栗抓住我的手臂。

sentences.en: 'That is not a coincidence,' she said.
sentences.cn: "这不是巧合，"她说。

awareness:2.en: The old signal tower held one message, burned into the wall in code: a map of Harbor City's hidden broadcast nodes. My *awareness* of the underground network grew with every line I read. Someone had spent years drawing this. Ali touched my arm. The map was still warm.
awareness:2.cnHint: 调查员在旧信号塔里发现了一幅地图，对地下广播网络的____逐渐加深。
awareness:2.hook: The last node on the map pointed straight to our safehouse.
awareness:2.line: 'My *awareness* of their network just doubled — look at this map.'

sentences.en: The old signal tower held one message, burned into the wall in code: a map of Harbor City's hidden broadcast nodes.
sentences.cn: 那座老信号塔的墙上用代码烧进去一条信息：港口城的隐藏广播节点地图。

sentences.en: My *awareness* of the underground network grew with every line I read.
Someone had spent years drawing this.
sentences.cn: 有人花了多年时间画出这张图。

sentences.en: Ali touched my arm.
sentences.cn: 阿栗碰了碰我的手臂。

sentences.en: The map was still warm.
sentences.cn: 地图还是热的。

introduce:2.en: Grey Crow left a data chip on the dead-drop bench. The file inside was titled: 'How to *introduce* a false signal into the city grid.' I read it twice. The method was clean, almost elegant. One wrong move, though, and every screen in Harbor City would go dark at once.
introduce:2.cnHint: 灰鸦留下了一块芯片，教调查员如何将假信号____到城市电网中。
introduce:2.hook: The last line of the file read: 'You have twelve hours.'
introduce:2.line: 'Use this to *introduce* a false signal — but only once.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow left a data chip on the dead-drop bench.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦在落地dead-drop长椅上留下了一枚数据芯片。

sentences.en: The file inside was titled: 'How to *introduce* a false signal into the city grid.'
I read it twice.
sentences.cn: 我读了两遍。

sentences.en: The method was clean, almost elegant.
sentences.cn: 方法很干净，几乎很优雅。

sentences.en: One wrong move, though, and every screen in Harbor City would go dark at once.
sentences.cn: 但要是出一步错，港口城的每块屏幕都会立刻黑掉。

expense:2.en: Ali found the receipt tucked inside a cracked terminal near Dock Nine. Every forbidden broadcast in the last month had been run at the *expense* of one anonymous account — drained to zero, then closed. Someone had paid a heavy price to keep the signals alive. The account name was a single word: Zero.
expense:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现了一张收据，所有非法广播都以某个账户为____运行，账户名正是零点。
expense:2.hook: The account had been reopened that same morning.
expense:2.line: 'All of it done at the *expense* of one account — Zero's account.'

sentences.en: Ali found the receipt tucked inside a cracked terminal near Dock Nine.
sentences.cn: 阿栗在九号码头附近一个裂开的终端机里找到了收据。

sentences.en: Every forbidden broadcast in the last month had been run at the *expense* of one anonymous account — drained to zero, then closed.
Someone had paid a heavy price to keep the signals alive.
sentences.cn: 有人付出了巨大代价来维持这些信号。

sentences.en: The account name was a single word: Zero.
sentences.cn: 账户名只有一个单词：零点。

toward:2.en: The encrypted letter arrived at my terminal just before dawn. Each sentence pushed *toward* a single conclusion: the city's language filter had a back door, and Grey Crow had built it. I printed the letter and held it under the cold light. The words did not change no matter how long I stared.
toward:2.cnHint: 一封加密信件将调查员的思路引导____一个结论：语言过滤器有一扇后门。
toward:2.hook: Grey Crow's signature was at the bottom — dated tomorrow.
toward:2.line: 'Every clue points *toward* the same answer — Grey Crow built the back door.'

sentences.en: The encrypted letter arrived at my terminal just before dawn.
sentences.cn: 那封加密信件在天亮前不久送到了我的终端机。

sentences.en: Each sentence pushed *toward* a single conclusion: the city's language filter had a back door, and Grey Crow had built it.
I printed the letter and held it under the cold light.
sentences.cn: 我把信打印出来，放在冷光下。

sentences.en: The words did not change no matter how long I stared.
sentences.cn: 我盯着再久，字都没有变过。

track:2.en: Buried in the station's old log files, I found a *track* of every signal Zero had ever sent — time, length, frequency, all recorded in neat rows. It was the kind of evidence that could end a career. Or start a war. Ali stood at the door, watching the corridor.
track:2.cnHint: 调查员在日志文件里找到了零点所有信号的____记录，这些证据足以引发一场风波。
track:2.hook: The most recent entry in the log was timestamped three minutes ago.
track:2.line: 'I found a full *track* of every signal Zero ever sent — it is all here.'

sentences.en: Buried in the station's old log files, I found a *track* of every signal Zero had ever sent — time, length, frequency, all recorded in neat rows.
It was the kind of evidence that could end a career.
sentences.cn: 这是能毁掉一个人职业生涯的证据。

sentences.en: Or start a war.
sentences.cn: 也是能引发一场战争的证据。

sentences.en: Ali stood at the door, watching the corridor.
sentences.cn: 阿栗站在门边，注视着走廊。

afford:2.en: The city archive was locked behind a pay wall — a hundred credits per query. I could only *afford* three searches before my account ran dry. I used the first on Zero's name, the second on the signal frequency, and held the third in reserve. The results from search two made my hand go still.
afford:2.cnHint: 调查员在城市档案馆只____得起三次查询，第二次的结果令他震惊。
afford:2.hook: Search two returned a single file marked: 'Destroy on read.'
afford:2.line: 'We can only *afford* three searches — choose them carefully.'

sentences.en: The city archive was locked behind a pay wall — a hundred credits per query.
sentences.cn: 城市档案库被设在付费墙后面——每次查询一百学分。

sentences.en: I could only *afford* three searches before my account ran dry.
I used the first on Zero's name, the second on the signal frequency, and held the third in reserve.
sentences.cn: 我用第一次查询了零点的名字，第二次查询了信号频率，留下第三次以防万一。

sentences.en: The results from search two made my hand go still.
sentences.cn: 第二次查询的结果让我的手停住了。

feature:2.en: Grey Crow's hidden note described one key *feature* of the cipher: it changed pattern every hour, on the hour, without fail. That meant any message sent at 11:58 would be unreadable by midnight. I checked the clock on the wall. It read 11:56.
feature:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的密码有一个关键____：每整点自动变换规律，调查员只剩两分钟破译。
feature:2.hook: The clock skipped a second — someone had slowed it down.
feature:2.line: 'The main *feature* of this cipher is that it resets every single hour.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow's hidden note described one key *feature* of the cipher: it changed pattern every hour, on the hour, without fail.
That meant any message sent at 11:58 would be unreadable by midnight.
sentences.cn: 那意味着任何在11点58分发送的信息到午夜就读不了了。

sentences.en: I checked the clock on the wall.
sentences.cn: 我看了一眼墙上的时钟。

sentences.en: It read 11:56.
sentences.cn: 显示的是11点56分。

innovative:2.en: The graffiti on the sub-level wall was unlike anything in the city database. Ali called it *innovative* — a new encoding layer woven inside ordinary paint strokes that no standard scanner could read. I pressed my palm flat against the wall and listened. A voice, thin as wire, told me where to go next.
innovative:2.cnHint: 地下通道的涂鸦采用了一种____的编码方式，调查员贴近墙壁时听到了指引。
innovative:2.hook: The voice said one name, then cut to silence: Zero.
innovative:2.line: 'This coding style is *innovative* — no city scanner will ever catch it.'

sentences.en: The graffiti on the sub-level wall was unlike anything in the city database.
sentences.cn: 地下室墙上的涂鸦在城市数据库里找不到。

sentences.en: Ali called it *innovative* — a new encoding layer woven inside ordinary paint strokes that no standard scanner could read.
I pressed my palm flat against the wall and listened.
sentences.cn: 我把手掌贴在墙上，静静聆听。

sentences.en: A voice, thin as wire, told me where to go next.
sentences.cn: 一个声音，细如电线，告诉我接下来该去哪里。

institution:2.en: The signal led me to a forgotten archive beneath Harbor City's oldest *institution* — a council hall sealed since 2041. Ali pressed her ear to the stone wall. Inside, something was still transmitting. Grey Crow had told me this place held the first language laws ever written. Now someone was rewriting them.
institution:2.cnHint: 信号将我引向这座城市最古老____地下室，那里似乎有人正在篡改最初的语言法则。
institution:2.hook: The broadcast cut out — then a new voice replaced Grey Crow's.
institution:2.line: 'This *institution* wrote the first rules. Now it hides the last ones.'

sentences.en: The signal led me to a forgotten archive beneath Harbor City's oldest *institution* — a council hall sealed since 2041.
Ali pressed her ear to the stone wall.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把耳朵贴在石墙上。

sentences.en: Inside, something was still transmitting.
sentences.cn: 里面，什么东西还在发射信号。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had told me this place held the first language laws ever written.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦告诉过我这个地方存放着历史上最早的语言法律。

sentences.en: Now someone was rewriting them.
sentences.cn: 现在有人在改写它们。

outcome:2.en: Ali decoded the third layer of Zero's message in under a minute. The *outcome* surprised us both: the signal was not a threat. It was a warning meant for us. Grey Crow had sent it six hours ago, before going silent. Someone had intercepted the original and changed two words.
outcome:2.cnHint: 阿栗破解信号后，____令我们震惊——那条消息其实是灰鸦发出的警告。
outcome:2.hook: Those two changed words pointed directly at my name.
outcome:2.line: 'The *outcome* of this message was never meant for Zero.'

sentences.en: Ali decoded the third layer of Zero's message in under a minute.
sentences.cn: 阿栗不到一分钟就破译了零点信息的第三层加密。

sentences.en: The *outcome* surprised us both: the signal was not a threat.
It was a warning meant for us.
sentences.cn: 这是一个警告，发给我们的。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had sent it six hours ago, before going silent.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦是在六个小时前发出的，之后就没有音讯了。

sentences.en: Someone had intercepted the original and changed two words.
sentences.cn: 有人截获了原信息，改了其中两个词。

recognize:2.en: I pulled the data chip from the wall panel and held it under the blue light. Grey Crow had taught me one thing: always check the edge code. I could *recognize* his signature pattern instantly — seven dots, one gap. But tonight the gap was in the wrong place. This chip was a copy.
recognize:2.cnHint: 我在蓝光下检查芯片，却发现我能____出灰鸦标记的细微差异——这是一个假冒品。
recognize:2.hook: The real chip was still out there, and Zero already had a head start.
recognize:2.line: 'I can *recognize* his mark anywhere — this one is wrong.'

sentences.en: I pulled the data chip from the wall panel and held it under the blue light.
sentences.cn: 我从墙壁面板上拔出数据芯片，放在蓝光下照。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had taught me one thing: always check the edge code.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦教过我一件事：总要检查边缘代码。

sentences.en: I could *recognize* his signature pattern instantly — seven dots, one gap.
But tonight the gap was in the wrong place.
sentences.cn: 但今晚那个间隔位置不对劲。

sentences.en: This chip was a copy.
sentences.cn: 这块芯片是复制品。

safety:2.en: Ali found the hidden room first. She waved me inside and bolted the door. The walls were lined with old broadcast equipment, all dark. A note on the desk read: 'Your *safety* ends when you transmit.' Grey Crow had written it. Below, in red ink, someone else had added: 'Too late.'
safety:2.cnHint: 我们躲进密室，桌上灰鸦留下的纸条提醒我们____岌岌可危，而红字留言说一切已经太迟。
safety:2.hook: The equipment on the wall began to hum on its own.
safety:2.line: 'Your *safety* depends on staying quiet — no transmissions, none.'

sentences.en: Ali found the hidden room first.
sentences.cn: 阿栗最先发现了那间隐藏的房间。

sentences.en: She waved me inside and bolted the door.
sentences.cn: 她挥手示意我进去，然后闩上了门。

sentences.en: The walls were lined with old broadcast equipment, all dark.
sentences.cn: 墙壁上装满了老式的广播设备，全都黑着。

sentences.en: A note on the desk read: 'Your *safety* ends when you transmit.'
Grey Crow had written it.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦写的。

sentences.en: Below, in red ink, someone else had added: 'Too late.'
sentences.cn: 下面用红墨笔有人又加了一句：太晚了。

collect:2.en: Zero had spent weeks learning to *collect* the forbidden signal fragments that drifted through Harbor City's lower channels. Each one alone meant nothing. Together, Ali whispered, they formed a map. Grey Crow had warned us someone was building that map. We never thought it would be finished this fast.
collect:2.cnHint: 零点花了数周时间____那些禁播信号碎片，而阿栗告诉我，拼在一起它们竟然构成了一张地图。
collect:2.hook: The map had only one destination marked, and it was my address.
collect:2.line: 'Zero will *collect* every fragment before dawn — we have hours.'

sentences.en: Zero had spent weeks learning to *collect* the forbidden signal fragments that drifted through Harbor City's lower channels.
Each one alone meant nothing.
sentences.cn: 每个单独的片段都毫无意义。

sentences.en: Together, Ali whispered, they formed a map.
sentences.cn: 阿栗低声说，它们拼在一起就组成了一张地图。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had warned us someone was building that map.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦警告过我们有人在绘制那张地图。

sentences.en: We never thought it would be finished this fast.
sentences.cn: 我们从没想过它会这么快完成。

door:2.en: The signal pulsed twice, then died. I traced it to a maintenance corridor on level nine. At the far end stood a steel *door* covered in coded graffiti — the same cipher Grey Crow had used in his last message. Ali read the symbols aloud. The door clicked open before she finished the final word.
door:2.cnHint: 我追踪信号来到一扇布满密码涂鸦的铁____，阿栗朗读符文时，门在她念完之前就自动开了。
door:2.hook: The room beyond was empty except for a single blinking light.
door:2.line: 'That *door* only opens for someone who knows the old cipher.'

sentences.en: The signal pulsed twice, then died.
sentences.cn: 信号脉冲了两下，然后消失了。

sentences.en: I traced it to a maintenance corridor on level nine.
sentences.cn: 我追踪到了九层的一条维修走廊。

sentences.en: At the far end stood a steel *door* covered in coded graffiti — the same cipher Grey Crow had used in his last message.
Ali read the symbols aloud.
sentences.cn: 阿栗大声读出了符号。

sentences.en: The door clicked open before she finished the final word.
sentences.cn: 她还没读完最后一个字，门就咔一声打开了。

eventually:2.en: Grey Crow had warned me that Zero's plan would *eventually* reach this block. I had not believed him. Ali pulled the latest intercept from her sleeve and read it quietly. Every route out of the archive was named. Every name on the list was ours. The plan had not just reached us — it had been waiting.
eventually:2.cnHint: 灰鸦曾警告过我，零点的计划____会蔓延到这里；现在截获的情报证明，它早已在等我们。
eventually:2.hook: There was a fourth name on the list — one I did not know.
eventually:2.line: 'It will *eventually* close in — Zero planned this street by street.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow had warned me that Zero's plan would *eventually* reach this block.
I had not believed him.
sentences.cn: 我没有相信他。

sentences.en: Ali pulled the latest intercept from her sleeve and read it quietly.
sentences.cn: 阿栗从袖子里掏出最新的截获信息，静静地读着。

sentences.en: Every route out of the archive was named.
sentences.cn: 档案库的每一条撤离路线都被列了出来。

sentences.en: Every name on the list was ours.
sentences.cn: 单子上的每个名字都是我们的。

sentences.en: The plan had not just reached us — it had been waiting.
sentences.cn: 这个计划不只是威胁到了我们——它早就在等我们。

match:2.en: Ali ran the voice print twice. Neither result would *match* the sample Grey Crow had given us. The broadcast signal was too clean, too steady — no human speaker was that precise. Zero had built something that could copy a voice down to the breath. Whatever was speaking on that channel was not alive.
match:2.cnHint: 阿栗两次比对声纹，结果都无法与样本____——零点造出了一个能完美复制人声的东西。
match:2.hook: Then the voice on the channel said my name.
match:2.line: 'Nothing should *match* that print this closely — nothing human.'

sentences.en: Ali ran the voice print twice.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把那份声纹分析跑了两遍。

sentences.en: Neither result would *match* the sample Grey Crow had given us.
The broadcast signal was too clean, too steady — no human speaker was that precise.
sentences.cn: 广播信号太干净了，太稳定了——没有人类说话能精确到这种程度。

sentences.en: Zero had built something that could copy a voice down to the breath.
sentences.cn: 零点造出了能把一个人的声音复制到每一次呼吸的东西。

sentences.en: Whatever was speaking on that channel was not alive.
sentences.cn: 那个频道里传出来的不是活物。

moment:2.en: The old signal tower on Pier Nine had been silent for years. Then, for one brief *moment*, every dead screen in the building lit up at once — all showing the same six-digit code. I copied it fast. The screens went dark again before Ali could reach the door.
moment:2.cnHint: 码头信号塔突然亮起，我在那个____里抄下了神秘编码。
moment:2.hook: The code matched the lock on Grey Crow's sealed file.
moment:2.line: 'That *moment* of light — it was meant for you alone,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: The old signal tower on Pier Nine had been silent for years.
sentences.cn: 九号码头上的老信号塔沉默了好多年。

sentences.en: Then, for one brief *moment*, every dead screen in the building lit up at once — all showing the same six-digit code.
I copied it fast.
sentences.cn: 我快速地抄了下来。

sentences.en: The screens went dark again before Ali could reach the door.
sentences.cn: 阿栗还没赶到门边，屏幕就全黑了。

nice:2.en: Zero had built the trap with *nice* precision: every wire spaced exactly two centimetres apart, every sensor tuned to a single body temperature. A rough plan would have failed. Only someone who understood the system at its deepest level could have threaded such a careful net around the archive room.
nice:2.cnHint: 零点设下的陷阱极为____，我差点踏入。
nice:2.hook: And the handwriting on the wiring diagram looked familiar.
nice:2.line: '*Nice* work — but you forgot I studied the same manual,' Ali said.

sentences.en: Zero had built the trap with *nice* precision: every wire spaced exactly two centimetres apart, every sensor tuned to a single body temperature.
A rough plan would have failed.
sentences.cn: 一个粗糙的计划早就失败了。

sentences.en: Only someone who understood the system at its deepest level could have threaded such a careful net around the archive room.
sentences.cn: 只有那种对系统有最深理解的人，才能在档案室周围织出这样精密的陷阱。

peer:2.en: I pressed my face to the frosted glass and tried to *peer* through the thick blur of light and shadow. A shape moved inside — tall, still, holding something flat against its chest. A folder, maybe. Or a weapon. I could not tell. Ali pulled my arm. 'Not yet,' she breathed.
peer:2.cnHint: 我透过磨砂玻璃____，隐约看见室内有人影移动。
peer:2.hook: The shape turned, as if it already knew I was there.
peer:2.line: '*Peer* any harder and they will see your breath on the glass,' Ali warned.

sentences.en: I pressed my face to the frosted glass and tried to *peer* through the thick blur of light and shadow.
A shape moved inside — tall, still, holding something flat against its chest.
sentences.cn: 里面有个身影动了一下——很高，很静止，胸前贴着什么平的东西。

sentences.en: A folder, maybe.
sentences.cn: 可能是个文件夹。

sentences.en: Or a weapon.
sentences.cn: 也可能是武器。

sentences.en: I could not tell.
sentences.cn: 我看不出来。

sentences.en: Ali pulled my arm.
sentences.cn: 阿栗拉了我的胳膊。

sentences.en: 'Not yet,' she breathed.
sentences.cn: 还不行，她低声说。

pretty:2.en: On the evidence table lay a small silver pin — the kind a street vendor might call a *pretty*, a cheap trinket, easy to ignore. But under the scanner it pulsed with a live signal, broadcasting a tight loop of encrypted audio. Someone had worn it inside the command hall. Someone trusted.
pretty:2.cnHint: 那枚看似普通____的别针，其实是一枚间谍信号器。
pretty:2.hook: The broadcast frequency matched Grey Crow's private channel.
pretty:2.line: 'A *pretty* is the best place to hide what no one wants to find,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: On the evidence table lay a small silver pin — the kind a street vendor might call a *pretty*, a cheap trinket, easy to ignore.
But under the scanner it pulsed with a live signal, broadcasting a tight loop of encrypted audio.
sentences.cn: 但在扫描仪下它闪烁着活跃的信号，循环播放着一段加密的音频。

sentences.en: Someone had worn it inside the command hall.
sentences.cn: 有人把它戴进了指挥厅。

sentences.en: Someone trusted.
sentences.cn: 某个信任度很高的人。

recommendation:2.en: Tucked inside the cracked data-pad was a single printed card — a *recommendation* letter, signed by the chief of city communications, vouching for an agent named only 'V'. No photo. No ID number. Just three lines of praise and a stamp that should not exist outside the sealed government archive.
recommendation:2.cnHint: 我在数据板里发现了一封____信，署名来自通讯局长。
recommendation:2.line: 'A *recommendation* from the chief means someone powerful opened that door,' Ali said.

sentences.en: Tucked inside the cracked data-pad was a single printed card — a *recommendation* letter, signed by the chief of city communications, vouching for an agent named only 'V'.
No photo.
sentences.cn: 没有照片。

sentences.en: No ID number.
sentences.cn: 没有身份号码。

sentences.en: Just three lines of praise and a stamp that should not exist outside the sealed government archive.
sentences.cn: 只有三行溢美之词和一枚本不该出现在密封政府档案库之外的印章。

strange:2.en: The maintenance log was full of *strange* entries — times that looped, rooms that did not appear on any map, names written and then crossed out in a different ink. I had never worked a case where the building itself seemed to be hiding something. Ali flagged three entries. All pointed to Sub-level Four.
strange:2.cnHint: 维护日志中出现了许多____记录，指向一个未知楼层。
strange:2.hook: Sub-level Four was listed as demolished six years ago.
strange:2.line: 'These *strange* timestamps all stop on the same night,' Ali said quietly.

sentences.en: The maintenance log was full of *strange* entries — times that looped, rooms that did not appear on any map, names written and then crossed out in a different ink.
I had never worked a case where the building itself seemed to be hiding something.
sentences.cn: 我从来没有接过这样的案子，建筑本身好像在隐瞒什么。

sentences.en: Ali flagged three entries.
sentences.cn: 阿栗标记了三条记录。

sentences.en: All pointed to Sub-level Four.
sentences.cn: 全都指向地下四层。

widespread:2.en: Grey Crow spread the city map across the floor. The red marks were *widespread* — docks, transit hubs, broadcast towers, even the water-processing plant. Zero had not built one trap. Zero had built a net that covered the entire city, and every node was set to trigger at the same second.
widespread:2.cnHint: 零点的部署____整座城市，每个节点将同时引爆。
widespread:2.hook: The trigger time was less than one hour away.
widespread:2.line: 'A plan this *widespread* needs someone inside every district,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: Grey Crow spread the city map across the floor.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦把城市地图铺在地板上。

sentences.en: The red marks were *widespread* — docks, transit hubs, broadcast towers, even the water-processing plant.
Zero had not built one trap.
sentences.cn: 零点不是造了一个陷阱。

sentences.en: Zero had built a net that covered the entire city, and every node was set to trigger at the same second.
sentences.cn: 零点造了一张覆盖整个城市的网，每个节点都设定在同一秒引爆。

wonderful:2.en: The hidden room smelled of old paper and warm circuitry. Every wall was covered in hand-drawn charts — a *wonderful* and terrible map of Harbor City's secret language network, years of work, each coded signal linked to a real name. Whoever built this room had already solved the case we were just beginning.
wonderful:2.cnHint: 密室的墙上布满图表，是一幅____而可怕的城市暗语全图。
wonderful:2.hook: At the centre of every chart was my own call-sign.
wonderful:2.line: '*Wonderful* — and it means someone has been watching us from the start,' said Grey Crow.

sentences.en: The hidden room smelled of old paper and warm circuitry.
sentences.cn: 隐藏房间里飘着纸张和温热电路的味道。

sentences.en: Every wall was covered in hand-drawn charts — a *wonderful* and terrible map of Harbor City's secret language network, years of work, each coded signal linked to a real name.
Whoever built this room had already solved the case we were just beginning.
sentences.cn: 无论谁建造了这个房间，都已经解决了我们才刚开始的案子。

safe:2.en: The old clock tower smelled of rust and dead signals. Ali pointed her light at the far wall. Behind a torn city map, bolted to the stone, sat a heavy iron *safe*. Its dial had been replaced with a keypad — and someone had already typed in three wrong codes. One more wrong guess would lock it forever.
safe:2.cnHint: 在钟楼破旧的石墙后，我们发现了一个铁制____，键盘上已有三次错误记录。
safe:2.hook: The fourth attempt would either open everything — or seal it shut.
safe:2.line: 'That *safe* has been here since before the city went dark,' Ali said.

sentences.en: The old clock tower smelled of rust and dead signals.
sentences.cn: 老钟楼里弥漫着铁锈和死信号的味道。

sentences.en: Ali pointed her light at the far wall.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把手电指向远处的墙。

sentences.en: Behind a torn city map, bolted to the stone, sat a heavy iron *safe*.
Its dial had been replaced with a keypad — and someone had already typed in three wrong codes.
sentences.cn: 拨盘被换成了键盘——已经有人输入了三个错误的密码。

sentences.en: One more wrong guess would lock it forever.
sentences.cn: 再错一次就永远锁死了。

speed:2.en: Grey Crow's message hit my receiver at 3:47 a.m.: coordinates, a sub-level drain pipe, and one word — hurry. I ran. The *speed* of the encrypted signal told me this was not a drill; high-frequency bursts only fired when time was nearly gone. I reached the pipe. A data chip lay in the shallow water, still warm.
speed:2.cnHint: 格雷·克罗的加密信号以极快的____传来，我知道这次不是演习。
speed:2.hook: The chip's last recorded timestamp was exactly three minutes from now.
speed:2.line: 'The *speed* of this signal means we have less time than you think,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: Grey Crow's message hit my receiver at 3:47 a.m.: coordinates, a sub-level drain pipe, and one word — hurry.
sentences.cn: 凌晨3点47分，灰鸦的信息打到我的接收器上：坐标、一条地下排水管，还有一个词——快。

sentences.en: I ran.
sentences.cn: 我跑了。

sentences.en: The *speed* of the encrypted signal told me this was not a drill; high-frequency bursts only fired when time was nearly gone.
I reached the pipe.
sentences.cn: 我到达了管道。

sentences.en: A data chip lay in the shallow water, still warm.
sentences.cn: 一块数据芯片躺在浅水里，还是温的。

burden:2.en: Ali dropped a sealed case on the table between us. Inside were twelve data drives — every stolen voice file Zero had collected for a year. 'These are yours now,' she said quietly. I felt the *burden* of that weight at once; each drive held a citizen's words, words that could free them or destroy them, depending on who decoded them first.
burden:2.cnHint: 阿里将十二块数据盘交给我，我立刻感受到这份沉重的____。
burden:2.hook: Somewhere in those drives was a voice I recognized as my own.
burden:2.line: 'Don't let this *burden* break you before you reach the end,' Ali said.

sentences.en: Ali dropped a sealed case on the table between us.
sentences.cn: 阿栗在我们之间的桌子上放下一个密封的箱子。

sentences.en: Inside were twelve data drives — every stolen voice file Zero had collected for a year.
sentences.cn: 里面是十二块数据盘——零点一年来收集的所有被盗音频文件。

sentences.en: 'These are yours now,' she said quietly.
sentences.cn: "这些现在是你的了，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: I felt the *burden* of that weight at once; each drive held a citizen's words, words that could free them or destroy them, depending on who decoded them first.

former:2.en: The note was pressed under a loose floor tile in the signal room. It listed two names: the current city censor, and a *former* one who had been reported dead two years ago. Below both names, in red ink, was a single question — who is still giving orders? I stared at the paper. The handwriting matched Grey Crow's exactly.
former:2.cnHint: 纸条上列着现任和____任审查官的名字，下面是一个令人不安的问题。
former:2.hook: If the former censor was alive, every case I had closed was built on a lie.
former:2.line: 'The *former* censor never actually left the city,' Grey Crow said softly.

sentences.en: The note was pressed under a loose floor tile in the signal room.
sentences.cn: 纸条被压在信号室的一块松动的地板砖下面。

sentences.en: It listed two names: the current city censor, and a *former* one who had been reported dead two years ago.
Below both names, in red ink, was a single question — who is still giving orders?
sentences.cn: 两个名字下面，用红墨水写着一个问题——谁还在下令？

sentences.en: I stared at the paper.
sentences.cn: 我盯着这张纸。

sentences.en: The handwriting matched Grey Crow's exactly.
sentences.cn: 笔迹和灰鸦的一模一样。

oppose:2.en: Zero had left a broadcast tag on every public screen in the lower district. The message was simple: anyone who tried to decode the city's forbidden channel would be traced. Ali wanted to pull the tags down. I told her to wait. To *oppose* Zero openly now, before we had the core file, would warn them and close our only window. She bit her lip and stepped back.
oppose:2.cnHint: 阿里想立刻行动，但我知道现在公开____零会让我们失去唯一的机会。
oppose:2.hook: Zero's next broadcast would go live in exactly forty minutes.
oppose:2.line: 'To *oppose* Zero without proof is just noise,' I told Ali.

sentences.en: Zero had left a broadcast tag on every public screen in the lower district.
sentences.cn: 零点在下城区的每块公共屏幕上留了一个广播标签。

sentences.en: The message was simple: anyone who tried to decode the city's forbidden channel would be traced.
sentences.cn: 信息很简单：任何试图解码城市禁频道的人都会被追踪。

sentences.en: Ali wanted to pull the tags down.
sentences.cn: 阿栗想把标签扯下来。

sentences.en: I told her to wait.
sentences.cn: 我让她等着。

sentences.en: To *oppose* Zero openly now, before we had the core file, would warn them and close our only window.
She bit her lip and stepped back.
sentences.cn: 她咬着嘴唇往后退了。

unable:2.en: I pressed play on the recovered audio log. Grey Crow's voice began, calm and clear — then cut to static halfway through a sentence. I replayed it four times. The gap was not a glitch; it was a deliberate cut. I was *unable* to hear the missing words, but the silence itself was shaped, filled with a frequency pattern I had never seen before. Someone had replaced sound with a coded signal.
unable:2.cnHint: 录音在关键处中断，我____听到那段缺失的内容，但沉默本身却藏着密码。
unable:2.hook: The coded silence lasted exactly as long as a name takes to speak.
unable:2.line: 'I am *unable* to verify who made that cut,' Grey Crow admitted.

sentences.en: I pressed play on the recovered audio log.
sentences.cn: 我按下恢复音频日志的播放键。

sentences.en: Grey Crow's voice began, calm and clear — then cut to static halfway through a sentence.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦的声音开始了，平静清晰——然后在一句话的中间变成了静电。

sentences.en: I replayed it four times.
sentences.cn: 我重放了四次。

sentences.en: The gap was not a glitch; it was a deliberate cut.
sentences.cn: 那个间断不是故障；是故意切掉的。

sentences.en: I was *unable* to hear the missing words, but the silence itself was shaped, filled with a frequency pattern I had never seen before.
Someone had replaced sound with a coded signal.
sentences.cn: 有人用编码信号替换了声音。

unusual:2.en: The sub-station log showed nothing wrong at first glance. But Ali flagged one entry: a maintenance window opened at 4:00 a.m. on a public holiday. *Unusual* enough to check. Behind that entry we found a hidden folder — twelve gig of city-wide listener data, sorted by neighborhood, tagged with a name I had only heard once before, in a warning Grey Crow gave me on my first day.
unusual:2.cnHint: 日志中一条____的维护记录引起了阿里的注意，背后藏着海量的监听数据。
unusual:2.hook: The name on those files was the last person I expected to find here.
unusual:2.line: 'This timing is *unusual* — no one runs maintenance on a holiday,' Ali said.

sentences.en: The sub-station log showed nothing wrong at first glance.
sentences.cn: 子站日志乍一看没什么问题。

sentences.en: But Ali flagged one entry: a maintenance window opened at 4:00 a.m. on a public holiday.
sentences.cn: 但阿栗标记了一条记录：公共假日的凌晨4点打开了一个维护窗口。

sentences.en: *Unusual* enough to check.

Behind that entry we found a hidden folder — twelve gig of city-wide listener data, sorted by neighborhood, tagged with a name I had only heard once before, in a warning Grey Crow gave me on my first day.
sentences.cn: 在那条记录后面，我们找到了一个隐藏文件夹——十二G的全城监听数据，按街区分类，标记着一个名字，我只在灰鸦新手时代给我的警告里听过一次。

apart:2.en: Grey Crow told me the two signal towers had always been linked. Tonight they were *apart* — operating on separate bands, sending different versions of the same city-wide message. One version told citizens to stay home. The other told them to gather at the harbor. Only someone standing between both signals, like me, could hear that the city itself was being told two different stories at once.
apart:2.cnHint: 两座信号塔今夜____运行，向市民广播着截然相反的指令。
apart:2.hook: I had to decide which version was the lie before dawn broke over the harbor.
apart:2.line: 'When these two towers are *apart*, the whole city splits,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: Grey Crow told me the two signal towers had always been linked.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦告诉我这两座信号塔一直是连接的。
