happiness:2.en: Ali found the child's drawing tucked inside the cracked wall panel — a sun, two figures holding hands, the word *happiness* written in unsteady letters below. In Harbor City, no child drew suns. The rain never stopped. This was a message. Someone had hidden it here on purpose, years ago, waiting.
happiness:2.cnHint: 阿栗在墙板里发现了一张画着太阳、写有____的儿童画，这显然是一条隐藏的信息。
happiness:2.hook: On the back, in tiny code, was a set of coordinates.
happiness:2.line: 'Someone hid the word *happiness* here because it was the last safe word left,' Ali said.

sentences.en: Ali found the child's drawing tucked inside the cracked wall panel — a sun, two figures holding hands, the word *happiness* written in unsteady letters below.
In Harbor City, no child drew suns.
sentences.cn: 在港城，没有孩子会画太阳。

sentences.en: The rain never stopped.
sentences.cn: 雨从不停歇。

sentences.en: This was a message.
sentences.cn: 这是一条信息。

sentences.en: Someone had hidden it here on purpose, years ago, waiting.
sentences.cn: 有人多年前故意把它藏在这里，在等待。

intelligent:2.en: Zero's trap was elegant — I had to admit it. Only a deeply *intelligent* mind could have built a false signal that looked real from every angle, that pulled us across three city sectors and cost us six hours. Grey Crow said nothing. They just looked at the empty room and nodded once, slowly.
intelligent:2.cnHint: 零点设下的陷阱极为精巧，让我不得不承认对手非常____。
intelligent:2.hook: And the real target had gone dark while we stood there.
intelligent:2.line: 'Zero is *intelligent* — smart enough to make us chase nothing,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: Zero's trap was elegant — I had to admit it.
sentences.cn: 得承认，零点的陷阱设计得精妙。

sentences.en: Only a deeply *intelligent* mind could have built a false signal that looked real from every angle, that pulled us across three city sectors and cost us six hours.
Grey Crow said nothing.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦什么都没说。

sentences.en: They just looked at the empty room and nodded once, slowly.
sentences.cn: 她只是看着空荡荡的房间，慢慢地点了一下头。

novel:2.en: The evidence locker held one item: a thin printed book, its cover blank. In 2099, no one printed books. The idea was *novel* enough to stop me cold. I opened it. Every page was filled not with words but with a dense grid of tiny symbols — a code I had never seen before. My pulse spiked.
novel:2.cnHint: 证物箱里有一本印刷书籍，这在2099年是件____的稀罕事，书页里全是未知符号。
novel:2.hook: The last page had my name on it, written by hand.
novel:2.line: 'A printed book — that's a *novel* way to hide a signal no one will scan,' Ali said.

sentences.en: The evidence locker held one item: a thin printed book, its cover blank.
sentences.cn: 证物柜里只有一件东西：一本薄薄的印刷书，封面空白。

sentences.en: In 2099, no one printed books.
sentences.cn: 在2099年，没人还在印刷书籍。

sentences.en: The idea was *novel* enough to stop me cold.
I opened it.
sentences.cn: 我打开了它。

sentences.en: Every page was filled not with words but with a dense grid of tiny symbols — a code I had never seen before.
sentences.cn: 每一页都不是文字，而是密密麻麻的微小符号组成的方阵——一种我从没见过的密码。

sentences.en: My pulse spiked.
sentences.cn: 我的心跳加速了。

political:2.en: Grey Crow spread the intercept on the table. The banned broadcast was not about crime or code — it was *political*, aimed straight at the city council, naming names. Releasing it would shake Harbor City to its roots. Zero had not built a weapon of steel. They had built a weapon of words.
political:2.cnHint: 被截获的广播内容是____性质的，直接点名批评市议会，零点以语言为武器。
political:2.hook: And someone had already sent a copy to every district tower.
political:2.line: 'This isn't a hack — it's *political*,' Grey Crow said, their voice flat and careful.

sentences.en: Grey Crow spread the intercept on the table.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦把截获的信息铺在桌子上。

sentences.en: The banned broadcast was not about crime or code — it was *political*, aimed straight at the city council, naming names.
Releasing it would shake Harbor City to its roots.
sentences.cn: 公开它会让港城震动。

sentences.en: Zero had not built a weapon of steel.
sentences.cn: 零点没有打造一件钢铁武器。

sentences.en: They had built a weapon of words.
sentences.cn: 他们打造的是言语之剑。

property:2.en: The deed was real — I ran the city seal twice. This entire block, twelve buildings, the old port gate, all of it was registered *property* of a shell name that traced back, after four layers, to Zero. They had been buying the city one quiet corner at a time. Not to live in it. To own the silence inside it.
property:2.cnHint: 这片街区的房产____全部登记在一个空壳名下，最终追溯到零点名下。
property:2.hook: The most recent purchase had closed at midnight — last night.
property:2.line: 'When you own the *property*, you own who gets to speak inside it,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: The deed was real — I ran the city seal twice.
sentences.cn: 契约是真的——我跑了两遍城市印鉴验证。

sentences.en: This entire block, twelve buildings, the old port gate, all of it was registered *property* of a shell name that traced back, after four layers, to Zero.
They had been buying the city one quiet corner at a time.
sentences.cn: 他们在一个安静的地方一个地方地买下整个城市。

sentences.en: Not to live in it.
sentences.cn: 不是为了住在里面。

sentences.en: To own the silence inside it.
sentences.cn: 是为了拥有那里面的沉默。

worldwide:2.en: The signal was not local. Grey Crow pulled up a map on her cracked screen, and I watched red dots bloom across every continent. The encrypted broadcast had gone *worldwide*, touching every city at once. Harbor City was just the first domino. Someone had planned this for years.
worldwide:2.cnHint: 加密广播已经____传播，港市只是第一块倒下的骨牌。
worldwide:2.hook: The next broadcast was already scheduled — in sixty seconds.
worldwide:2.line: 'This signal went *worldwide* before we even woke up.'

sentences.en: The signal was not local.
sentences.cn: 信号不是本地的。

sentences.en: Grey Crow pulled up a map on her cracked screen, and I watched red dots bloom across every continent.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦在她破旧的屏幕上打开了一张地图，我看着红点在每一个大陆上绽开。

sentences.en: The encrypted broadcast had gone *worldwide*, touching every city at once.
Harbor City was just the first domino.
sentences.cn: 港城只是第一张骨牌。

sentences.en: Someone had planned this for years.
sentences.cn: 有人为这一刻策划了多年。

accomplish:2.en: The server room was cold and silent. Ali knelt beside a broken terminal and rewired it with steady hands. 'Almost,' she whispered. She needed three more minutes to *accomplish* the data transfer before Zero's lock-code sealed every file forever. I stood watch at the door, barely breathing.
accomplish:2.cnHint: 阿栗正在争分夺秒地____数据传输，但时间所剩无几。
accomplish:2.hook: The lock-code counter hit thirty seconds and started falling fast.
accomplish:2.line: 'We can still *accomplish* this — just keep that door shut.'

sentences.en: The server room was cold and silent.
sentences.cn: 服务器室冷得要命，静得吓人。

sentences.en: Ali knelt beside a broken terminal and rewired it with steady hands.
sentences.cn: 阿栗跪在一台坏掉的终端前，用稳定的手法重新接好线路。

sentences.en: 'Almost,' she whispered.
sentences.cn: "快了，"她低声说。

sentences.en: She needed three more minutes to *accomplish* the data transfer before Zero's lock-code sealed every file forever.
I stood watch at the door, barely breathing.
sentences.cn: 我守在门边，几乎没有呼吸。

address:2.en: Hidden inside the stolen data chip was a single line of text: an *address* — a warehouse number on the dead end of Pier Nine. Grey Crow read it twice and said nothing. I had walked past that pier every night for a month without knowing what was inside. Someone had wanted me close all along.
address:2.cnHint: 数据芯片里藏着一个____，就在我每天路过的地方。
address:2.hook: The warehouse light was already on, and a shadow moved behind the glass.
address:2.line: 'That *address* — I know that place. We should not go alone.'

sentences.en: Hidden inside the stolen data chip was a single line of text: an *address* — a warehouse number on the dead end of Pier Nine.
Grey Crow read it twice and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦读了两遍，什么都没说。

sentences.en: I had walked past that pier every night for a month without knowing what was inside.
sentences.cn: 一个月来我每晚都走过那个码头，却从不知道里面藏着什么。

sentences.en: Someone had wanted me close all along.
sentences.cn: 有人一直想让我靠近。

barely:2.en: Zero's jamming signal hit the moment I opened the file. My earpiece screamed static. I could *barely* make out Grey Crow's voice cutting through the noise — three words, then silence. The neon outside the window flickered and died. Whatever she had tried to warn me about was already in the room.
barely:2.cnHint: 干扰信号骤然袭来，我____能听清灰鸦说了什么。
barely:2.hook: Something moved in the dark corner behind the server rack.
barely:2.line: 'I can *barely* hear you — say that last part again, fast.'

sentences.en: Zero's jamming signal hit the moment I opened the file.
sentences.cn: 零点的干扰信号在我打开文件的那一刻袭来。

sentences.en: My earpiece screamed static.
sentences.cn: 耳机里尖啸着静电噪音。

sentences.en: I could *barely* make out Grey Crow's voice cutting through the noise — three words, then silence.
The neon outside the window flickered and died.
sentences.cn: 窗外的霓虹灯闪烁了一下，熄灭了。

sentences.en: Whatever she had tried to warn me about was already in the room.
sentences.cn: 她试图警告我的事已经在房间里了。

blame:2.en: The evidence file named me as the leak. My ID, my access code, my route through the lower grid — all of it laid out in clean columns. Ali stared at the screen and would not look at me. I knew who had built this trap, but knowing was not the same as proof. Zero had made sure the *blame* would land on me alone.
blame:2.cnHint: 证据文件精心伪造，所有的____都指向了我。
blame:2.hook: Ali's hand moved slowly toward the alarm switch on the wall.
blame:2.line: 'Zero made sure all the *blame* points at you — we need proof now.'

sentences.en: The evidence file named me as the leak.
sentences.cn: 证据文件把泄密者指向了我。

sentences.en: My ID, my access code, my route through the lower grid — all of it laid out in clean columns.
sentences.cn: 我的ID、我的通行码、我穿过下层网格的路线——全都整整齐齐地列在表格里。

sentences.en: Ali stared at the screen and would not look at me.
sentences.cn: 阿栗盯着屏幕，不敢看我。

sentences.en: I knew who had built this trap, but knowing was not the same as proof.
sentences.cn: 我知道谁设的这个陷阱，但知道不等于有证据。

sentences.en: Zero had made sure the *blame* would land on me alone.

chat:2.en: The meet was supposed to be a quick *chat* in the back booth of the noodle shop on Level Six. Grey Crow was already there, hood up, eyes on the door. She slid a folded paper across the table before I even sat down. No words. Whatever she had written was too dangerous to say out loud in Harbor City.
chat:2.cnHint: 在六层面馆，一次简短的____却以一张危险的纸条告终。
chat:2.hook: The paper contained a name I had hoped never to read again.
chat:2.line: 'This was meant to be a quiet *chat* — so why is Zero outside?'

sentences.en: The meet was supposed to be a quick *chat* in the back booth of the noodle shop on Level Six.
Grey Crow was already there, hood up, eyes on the door.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦已经在那儿了，兜帽盖住了头，眼睛钉在门上。

sentences.en: She slid a folded paper across the table before I even sat down.
sentences.cn: 我还没坐下，她就把折好的纸条滑过了桌子。

sentences.en: No words.
sentences.cn: 没有一句话。

sentences.en: Whatever she had written was too dangerous to say out loud in Harbor City.
sentences.cn: 无论她写了什么，在港城说出来都太危险了。

combat:2.en: Grey Crow had spent years in signal *combat* — the silent war fought with codes, not fists. She had told me once that the sharpest weapon was a word the other side had never heard before. Tonight she uploaded a single forbidden phrase into Zero's broadcast loop. I watched his entire network stall and go dark.
combat:2.cnHint: 灰鸦用一句禁语展开信号____，让零点的网络陷入瘫痪。
combat:2.hook: Zero's reply came back in four seconds — colder and stranger than before.
combat:2.line: 'Signal *combat* is what I do best — stand back and watch.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow had spent years in signal *combat* — the silent war fought with codes, not fists.
She had told me once that the sharpest weapon was a word the other side had never heard before.
sentences.cn: 她曾经告诉我，最锋利的武器是对方从未听过的一个词。

sentences.en: Tonight she uploaded a single forbidden phrase into Zero's broadcast loop.
sentences.cn: 今晚她把一句禁言上传进了零点的广播循环。

sentences.en: I watched his entire network stall and go dark.
sentences.cn: 我看着他整个网络卡住了，陷入了黑暗。

danger:2.en: The note was tucked under the wiper of Ali's beat-up scooter, three floors below street level. Two words in red ink: real *danger*. Ali photographed it without touching it. We had kept our plan to four people. That meant one of them was feeding information to the other side, and the note was meant as a warning — or a taunt.
danger:2.cnHint: 停车场的一张纸条写着真实的____，四人小组里出现了内鬼。
danger:2.hook: Ali's phone buzzed — a message from the number that sent the note.
danger:2.line: 'When someone writes real *danger* in red, you do not ignore it.'

sentences.en: The note was tucked under the wiper of Ali's beat-up scooter, three floors below street level.
sentences.cn: 纸条塞在阿栗那辆破旧摩托车的雨刷下，在地下三层。

sentences.en: Two words in red ink: real *danger*.
Ali photographed it without touching it.
sentences.cn: 阿栗拍了照，没有碰它。

sentences.en: We had kept our plan to four people.
sentences.cn: 我们把计划只告诉了四个人。

sentences.en: That meant one of them was feeding information to the other side, and the note was meant as a warning — or a taunt.
sentences.cn: 这意味着其中一个在向对方泄露信息，纸条既是警告，也是嘲笑。

obvious:2.en: The message was hidden inside a torn poster on the wet wall of Sub-Level Nine. To anyone else it looked like faded ink. But to me the signal was *obvious*: three red dots, a pause, two blue lines — Grey Crow's private code. Someone had been here minutes ago. The ink was still damp.
obvious:2.cnHint: 我在九层地下通道的破海报里发现了一条隐藏信息，那个____的暗号告诉我灰鸦刚刚离开。
obvious:2.hook: But the footprints in the dust led the wrong way.
obvious:2.line: 'The pattern is *obvious* — Grey Crow left this for us alone.'

sentences.en: The message was hidden inside a torn poster on the wet wall of Sub-Level Nine.
sentences.cn: 信息藏在第九地下层湿漉漉的墙上一张破旧海报的里面。

sentences.en: To anyone else it looked like faded ink.
sentences.cn: 对别人来说只是褪了色的墨迹。

sentences.en: But to me the signal was *obvious*: three red dots, a pause, two blue lines — Grey Crow's private code.
Someone had been here minutes ago.
sentences.cn: 有人在几分钟前来过这里。

sentences.en: The ink was still damp.
sentences.cn: 墨迹还没干。

ordinary:2.en: Ali slid the object across the table: a small grey card, the kind handed out at every city checkpoint. It looked completely *ordinary*. No chip, no glow, no mark. Then I pressed my thumb to the corner and felt a faint hum. Hidden data, buried deep. Zero had found a way to weaponize the invisible.
ordinary:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给我一张看起来____的灰色通行卡，但它藏着连扫描仪都查不到的数据。
ordinary:2.hook: The hum stopped — and the card went cold.
ordinary:2.line: 'It looks *ordinary*, but hold it longer and you will feel it.'

sentences.en: Ali slid the object across the table: a small grey card, the kind handed out at every city checkpoint.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把东西滑过桌子：一张小小的灰色卡片，每个城市检查站都会发的那种。

sentences.en: It looked completely *ordinary*.
No chip, no glow, no mark.
sentences.cn: 没有芯片，没有光，没有标记。

sentences.en: Then I pressed my thumb to the corner and felt a faint hum.
sentences.cn: 然后我把大拇指按在角落，感到了一阵微弱的嗡鸣。

sentences.en: Hidden data, buried deep.
sentences.cn: 隐藏的数据，埋得很深。

sentences.en: Zero had found a way to weaponize the invisible.
sentences.cn: 零点找到了让无形的东西变成武器的办法。

pace:2.en: I began to *pace* the narrow server room, counting tiles, counting seconds. Grey Crow's last broadcast had said: wait for the third echo. Two had come. The rain hammered the roof. Somewhere in the walls, a signal was building, growing louder only I could hear it. The third echo was close.
pace:2.cnHint: 我在狭小的服务器室里____，等待灰鸦广播中提到的第三次回响信号。
pace:2.hook: Then every screen in the room went black at once.
pace:2.line: 'Stop — don't *pace* — stand still and listen for the third echo.'

sentences.en: I began to *pace* the narrow server room, counting tiles, counting seconds.
Grey Crow's last broadcast had said: wait for the third echo.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦的上一条广播说：等第三次回声。

sentences.en: Two had come.
sentences.cn: 已经来了两次。

sentences.en: The rain hammered the roof.
sentences.cn: 雨敲打着屋顶。

sentences.en: Somewhere in the walls, a signal was building, growing louder only I could hear it.
sentences.cn: 墙壁里的某个地方，一个信号在积聚、放大，只有我能听见它变得越来越响。

sentences.en: The third echo was close.
sentences.cn: 第三次回声快来了。

participate:2.en: The encrypted file listed twelve names. Mine was not there. Ali pointed to the gap at line seven — a blank where a name had been removed. Grey Crow had asked us to *participate* in the final operation, but someone had already erased our roles. We were being cut out before we even began.
participate:2.cnHint: 加密文件显示我们被人从最终行动的____名单里提前抹去了。
participate:2.hook: Line seven still carried a ghost signature — Zero's.
participate:2.line: 'We were chosen to *participate*, so why is our entry gone?'

sentences.en: The encrypted file listed twelve names.
sentences.cn: 加密文件里列了十二个名字。

sentences.en: Mine was not there.
sentences.cn: 我的不在里面。

sentences.en: Ali pointed to the gap at line seven — a blank where a name had been removed.
sentences.cn: 阿栗指着第七行的空白——一个被删除的名字留下的空位。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had asked us to *participate* in the final operation, but someone had already erased our roles.
We were being cut out before we even began.
sentences.cn: 我们还没开始就被踢出局了。

pilot:2.en: The transit pod sat dark in Bay Four, its door cracked open. Ali checked the control log: last *pilot* logged out six hours ago, but the seat was warm. Someone had guided this pod off-grid and come back on foot. The route it had taken led straight to the signal tower Grey Crow had warned us about.
pilot:2.cnHint: 停机坪的飞行舱座椅还有余温，上一位____六小时前登出，但有人悄悄开走又步行返回。
pilot:2.hook: The destination was still locked in the navigation memory.
pilot:2.line: 'A *pilot* left this pod warm — they came back for something they forgot.'

sentences.en: The transit pod sat dark in Bay Four, its door cracked open.
sentences.cn: 过境舱停在第四号船坞，舱门半开着。

sentences.en: Ali checked the control log: last *pilot* logged out six hours ago, but the seat was warm.
Someone had guided this pod off-grid and come back on foot.
sentences.cn: 有人把这艘舱驾离了网格，然后步行返回。

sentences.en: The route it had taken led straight to the signal tower Grey Crow had warned us about.
sentences.cn: 它走过的路线直指灰鸦警告我们的信号塔。

primary:2.en: Grey Crow's note was brief: three words and a grid number. Ali read it twice, then nodded. The grid pointed to the *primary* relay tower on the north ridge — the one node that all city broadcasts passed through. Whoever held that tower tonight held every word spoken in Harbor City.
primary:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的纸条指向北岭的____中继塔——控制它就等于控制全城的信号。
primary:2.hook: The tower's access light was already green; someone had arrived first.
primary:2.line: 'The *primary* relay is the key — lose it and we lose every channel.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow's note was brief: three words and a grid number.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦的纸条很简洁：三个词和一个网格号。

sentences.en: Ali read it twice, then nodded.
sentences.cn: 阿栗读了两遍，然后点了点头。

sentences.en: The grid pointed to the *primary* relay tower on the north ridge — the one node that all city broadcasts passed through.
Whoever held that tower tonight held every word spoken in Harbor City.
sentences.cn: 无论谁今晚控制了那座塔，就控制了港城里说出的每一个字。

priority:2.en: Ali pulled up the task list on the cracked screen. Four targets, four windows, one team. I crossed out two and circled the signal archive. Grey Crow had been clear: the archive was the *priority*. Everything else was noise. Zero knew it too — which meant we had maybe twenty minutes before they reached it.
priority:2.cnHint: 灰鸦明确说信号档案室是____，我们必须在零点抵达前的二十分钟内行动。
priority:2.hook: Ali checked the clock — nineteen minutes, now eighteen.
priority:2.line: 'Forget the rest — the archive is our *priority* and the clock is running.'

sentences.en: Ali pulled up the task list on the cracked screen.
sentences.cn: 阿栗在裂开的屏幕上拉出了任务清单。

sentences.en: Four targets, four windows, one team.
sentences.cn: 四个目标，四个时间窗口，一个小队。

sentences.en: I crossed out two and circled the signal archive.
sentences.cn: 我划掉了两个，圈出了信号档案库。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had been clear: the archive was the *priority*.
Everything else was noise.
sentences.cn: 其他都只是噪音。

sentences.en: Zero knew it too — which meant we had maybe twenty minutes before they reached it.
sentences.cn: 零点也知道——这意味着我们最多还有二十分钟才能抢到那里。

throughout:2.en: The hidden message was not a single line. It was scattered *throughout* the entire wall of code Grey Crow had sent — one letter per block, one block per minute, broadcast over three hours. Ali found the pattern first. Stitched together, the letters formed two words: Trust no one. We looked at each other in the cold blue light.
throughout:2.cnHint: 灰鸦发来的代码____藏着逐字拼出的隐秘信息，阿栗率先破译，结果令我们面面相觑。
throughout:2.hook: The last block had just arrived — and it added one more word.
throughout:2.line: 'The warning runs *throughout* the whole file — every block, every minute.'

sentences.en: The hidden message was not a single line.
sentences.cn: 隐藏的信息不是一行字。

sentences.en: It was scattered *throughout* the entire wall of code Grey Crow had sent — one letter per block, one block per minute, broadcast over three hours.
Ali found the pattern first.
sentences.cn: 阿栗最先发现了规律。

sentences.en: Stitched together, the letters formed two words: Trust no one.
sentences.cn: 把那些字母拼在一起，就是两个词：不信任何人。

sentences.en: We looked at each other in the cold blue light.
sentences.cn: 我们在冷蓝色的灯光下互相看着。

dinner:2.en: The tip said: server room, sub-level four. I pushed open a rusted door and found a long table set for twelve — cold plates, dead candles, untouched glasses. Someone had planned a *dinner* here and never come back. A folded note under the centrepiece read: 'They left without us.'
dinner:2.cnHint: 我在地下室发现一桌无人赴约的____，桌上留有一张纸条。
dinner:2.hook: The chair at the head was still warm.
dinner:2.line: 'This *dinner* was meant for people who no longer exist,' Ali said.

sentences.en: The tip said: server room, sub-level four.
sentences.cn: 线索说：服务器房间，地下四层。

sentences.en: I pushed open a rusted door and found a long table set for twelve — cold plates, dead candles, untouched glasses.
sentences.cn: 我推开一扇生锈的门，发现一张长桌，上面摆着十二个位置——冷盘子、死了的蜡烛、没碰过的玻璃杯。

sentences.en: Someone had planned a *dinner* here and never come back.
A folded note under the centrepiece read: 'They left without us.'
sentences.cn: 中心摆件下压着一张折起来的纸条，上面写着："他们丢下我们走了。"

embrace:2.en: Grey Crow spread a cracked city map across the floor. 'Harbor City doesn't just hold its secrets,' he said quietly. 'It *embraces* them — wraps them in concrete and rain until no one remembers to ask.' I stared at the red circles he had drawn and felt the city closing around me.
embrace:2.cnHint: 灰鸦解释说这座城市会____它的秘密，我盯着地图上的红圈感到窒息。
embrace:2.hook: One red circle was drawn around my own address.
embrace:2.line: 'A city that *embraces* its lies will never let you leave,' said Grey Crow.

sentences.en: Grey Crow spread a cracked city map across the floor.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦把一张裂纹城市地图铺在地板上。

sentences.en: 'Harbor City doesn't just hold its secrets,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "港城不只是藏着秘密，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: 'It *embraces* them — wraps them in concrete and rain until no one remembers to ask.'
I stared at the red circles he had drawn and felt the city closing around me.
sentences.cn: 我盯着他画的那些红圈，感觉城市在慢慢包围我。

explanation:2.en: Ali slid a data chip across the wet table. The file inside held three hundred names and no *explanation* — no date, no sender, no reason. Just names. I scrolled to the bottom and stopped breathing. The last entry was mine, added four minutes ago.

explanation:2.line: 'No *explanation* means they want you scared, not informed,' Ali said.

intend:2.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every channel at midnight. His voice was flat and certain: 'I *intend* to erase the last clean signal in Harbor City before dawn.' Grey Crow killed the radio with one hand. The silence that followed felt like a countdown none of us could see.
intend:2.cnHint: 零点在广播中宣布他____在天亮前摧毁最后的干净信号。
intend:2.hook: Grey Crow's other hand was already reaching for the door.
intend:2.line: 'I *intend* to finish this tonight — with or without your help,' Zero said.

leadership:2.en: Deep in the archive server I found a single photograph: twelve figures in grey coats standing in a half-circle. A burned label on the back read 'Original *Leadership* — Year One.' Every face had been scratched out except one. I recognised the jaw line immediately.

leadership:2.hook: That one remaining face belonged to someone I trusted.
leadership:2.line: 'The *leadership* was never dismantled — it just went underground,' Grey Crow said.

locate:2.en: Ali pressed two fingers to her earpiece and went still. 'I can *locate* the original broadcast tower,' she said slowly, 'but it's moving.' Towers don't move. I pulled up the signal map and watched a blinking dot drift through the old port district like a slow, deliberate heartbeat.

locate:2.line: '*Locate* the signal first; ask questions after,' Ali said.

original:2.en: The document Grey Crow handed me was printed on paper — actual paper, rare as silence in Harbor City. 'This is the *original* order,' he said. 'Not a copy, not a echo-file. The thing itself.' I turned it over. The ink was still slightly wet.

overcome:2.en: The signal jammer filled the corridor with a wall of white noise. My vision blurred and my legs felt like wet concrete. I pressed my back to the wall and counted breaths. Slowly, steadily, I *overcame* the pressure and stepped forward into the dark server hall alone.

throw:2.en: Ali found the data chip inside a cracked teacup on the dockside market stall. No label. No sender. Bringing it to Grey Crow felt like a *throw* of the dice — we had nothing else, and the city was closing in fast. Grey Crow held it to the light and said nothing for a long time.

unlike:2.en: The second letter was folded inside a hollow street lamp near the old harbor gate. I opened it in the rain. The handwriting was careful and small — *unlike* Zero's usual sharp, broken letters. Someone else had written this. Someone who wanted to help, or wanted us to think they did.

absolutely:2.en: Ali decoded the last layer of the file at dawn. The result was clean and clear: the forbidden broadcast had originated from inside City Hall. I stared at the screen. Grey Crow had told us to trust the data, and the data was *absolutely* certain. There was no other reading.

accumulate:2.en: For three weeks I had been collecting fragments: a word on a wall, a tone in a broadcast, a pattern in the city's rain-sensor data. Alone, each piece meant nothing. But evidence had begun to *accumulate*, and the shape it formed pointed to one name, one plan, one night.

accumulate:2.line: 'Let the clues *accumulate* — we move only when the picture is full,' Grey Crow said.

partly:2.cnHint: 码头下方的数据库房被____淹没，叙述者发现储物盒的锁已被剪断。
partly:2.hook: A wet footprint on the stairs was still fresh.
partly:2.line: 'The vault is *partly* open — someone left in a hurry.'

sentences.en: The old data vault under Pier Nine was *partly* flooded, water rising to my knees.
Grey Crow had said the drive was sealed inside a locked box on the lower shelf.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦说那块驱动器被锁在下层货架上的一个密封盒里。

sentences.en: I found the box.
sentences.cn: 我找到了那个盒子。

sentences.en: The lock was already cut.
sentences.cn: 锁已经被割开了。

sentences.en: Someone had been here before me, and they had not taken everything — which meant they would be back.
sentences.cn: 有人在我之前来过这儿，他们没有把所有东西都拿走——这意味着他们会回来。

practical:2.en: Ali spread the stolen city map across a dry pipe and tapped three circles in red ink. 'Forget the fancy routes,' she said. The most *practical* path to Zero's relay tower cut straight through the old market, no cameras, no checkpoints. It was also the path Grey Crow had told us never to use. We took it anyway.
practical:2.cnHint: 阿栗找到一条____的路线穿越旧市场，但那正是灰鸦警告过的禁忌路线。
practical:2.hook: Halfway through the market, every stall light went dark at once.
practical:2.line: 'This is the most *practical* route — trust the map, not the warning.'

sentences.en: Ali spread the stolen city map across a dry pipe and tapped three circles in red ink.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把偷来的城市地图铺在一根干燥的管子上，用红墨笔点了三个圆圈。

sentences.en: 'Forget the fancy routes,' she said.
sentences.cn: "别走什么花哨的路线，"她说。

sentences.en: The most *practical* path to Zero's relay tower cut straight through the old market, no cameras, no checkpoints.
It was also the path Grey Crow had told us never to use.
sentences.cn: 这也是灰鸦告诉我们永远不要走的那条路。

sentences.en: We took it anyway.
sentences.cn: 我们还是走了。

profit:2.en: The encrypted ledger on the cracked tablet showed one word repeated beside each transaction: SIGNAL. Grey Crow had suspected it for months. Zero was not selling data for money. The real *profit* was silence — every buyer received a forbidden word removed from the city's live broadcast feed forever. Someone was buying language itself out of existence.
profit:2.cnHint: 账本揭示零点的真正____不是金钱，而是将禁忌词从城市广播中永久抹去。
profit:2.hook: My own name appeared at the bottom of the list.
profit:2.line: 'The *profit* here is not money — it is erasure.'

sentences.en: The encrypted ledger on the cracked tablet showed one word repeated beside each transaction: SIGNAL.
sentences.cn: 破裂平板上的加密账本显示，每笔交易旁边都重复出现同一个词：信号。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had suspected it for months.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦已经怀疑了好几个月。

sentences.en: Zero was not selling data for money.
sentences.cn: 零点不是在卖数据换钱。

sentences.en: The real *profit* was silence — every buyer received a forbidden word removed from the city's live broadcast feed forever.
Someone was buying language itself out of existence.
sentences.cn: 有人在把语言本身从世界上买走。

promise:2.en: Grey Crow left a single folded note inside the hollow streetlight at Block Seven. The paper held one sentence: 'I made a *promise* to keep you out of the deep grid.' Below it, in smaller letters: 'I broke it. Go to the east tower before dawn.' I had never seen Grey Crow admit a mistake before. That scared me more than Zero ever had.
promise:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在路灯里留下纸条，承认打破了一个____，要求叙述者天亮前赶到东塔。
promise:2.hook: The note dissolved in my hand — reactive ink, thirty seconds of life.
promise:2.line: 'That *promise* I made — I could not keep it. Forgive me.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow left a single folded note inside the hollow streetlight at Block Seven.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦在七街区的空心路灯里留了一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: The paper held one sentence: 'I made a *promise* to keep you out of the deep grid.'
Below it, in smaller letters: 'I broke it.
sentences.cn: 下面用更小的字写着："我破了。

sentences.en: Go to the east tower before dawn.'
sentences.cn: 天亮前去东塔。"

sentences.en: I had never seen Grey Crow admit a mistake before.
sentences.cn: 我从没见过灰鸦承认错误。

sentences.en: That scared me more than Zero ever had.
sentences.cn: 那比零点曾经吓过我的任何事都更让我害怕。

rarely:2.en: The signal room on the fourteenth floor was *rarely* used; the dust on the console proved it. But tonight every screen was alive, scrolling names — investigators, informants, street readers like me. Ali grabbed my arm. Zero had not been hiding data. Zero had been building a list. Our names were near the top.
rarely:2.cnHint: 这个____使用的信号室今夜却亮起所有屏幕，显示着包括叙述者名字在内的目标名单。
rarely:2.hook: The door behind us clicked — a lock engaging, not opening.
rarely:2.line: 'This room is *rarely* lit. Tonight it is. Run.'

sentences.en: The signal room on the fourteenth floor was *rarely* used; the dust on the console proved it.
But tonight every screen was alive, scrolling names — investigators, informants, street readers like me.
sentences.cn: 但今晚每块屏幕都亮着，滚动着名字——调查员、线人、像我这样的街道读者。

sentences.en: Ali grabbed my arm.
sentences.cn: 阿栗抓住我的手臂。

sentences.en: Zero had not been hiding data.
sentences.cn: 零点不是在隐藏数据。

sentences.en: Zero had been building a list.
sentences.cn: 零点一直在建一份名单。

sentences.en: Our names were near the top.
sentences.cn: 我们的名字在前面。

severe:2.en: The warning carved into the relay box was short: SEVERE PENALTY FOR SIGNAL THEFT. I had read it a hundred times and ignored it. Tonight the box was open, the penalty already in motion — a dead-man signal broadcasting my ID to every city monitor in range. Grey Crow had said the system was *severe* without mercy. I had exactly four minutes to prove that wrong.
severe:2.cnHint: 继电器盒发出叙述者的身份信号，这套____的惩罚系统给了他们仅仅四分钟的逃跑时间。
severe:2.hook: Three minutes fifty seconds — and the elevator was out.
severe:2.line: 'The system is *severe* — four minutes is all you have.'

sentences.en: The warning carved into the relay box was short: SEVERE PENALTY FOR SIGNAL THEFT.
sentences.cn: 中继盒上刻的警告很简短：信号窃取将受严厉处罚。

sentences.en: I had read it a hundred times and ignored it.
sentences.cn: 我读过无数次，都没在乎。

sentences.en: Tonight the box was open, the penalty already in motion — a dead-man signal broadcasting my ID to every city monitor in range.
sentences.cn: 今晚这个盒子开着，处罚已经启动了——一个死人信号向所有范围内的城市监控广播我的身份。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had said the system was *severe* without mercy.
I had exactly four minutes to prove that wrong.
sentences.cn: 我只有四分钟时间来证明那是错的。

smell:2.en: The *smell* hit me first — burnt plastic and cold rain — before I even reached the sub-basement door. Inside, Zero's portable broadcast unit lay in pieces on the floor. The destruction was clean, deliberate. Ali knelt and touched the wire ends. 'Still warm,' she said quietly. Whoever had been here had left less than ten minutes ago, and they had not gone far.
smell:2.cnHint: 叙述者闻到烧焦的____，发现零点的广播设备被人刻意破坏，且破坏者刚刚离开。
smell:2.hook: Above us, slow and steady, came the sound of footsteps.
smell:2.line: 'That *smell* — burnt wire. Someone destroyed it on purpose.'

sentences.en: The *smell* hit me first — burnt plastic and cold rain — before I even reached the sub-basement door.
Inside, Zero's portable broadcast unit lay in pieces on the floor.
sentences.cn: 里面，零点的便携式广播装置散落在地板上。

sentences.en: The destruction was clean, deliberate.
sentences.cn: 破坏很干净，很刻意。

sentences.en: Ali knelt and touched the wire ends.
sentences.cn: 阿栗跪下来摸了摸电线的两端。

sentences.en: 'Still warm,' she said quietly.
sentences.cn: "还是热的，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: Whoever had been here had left less than ten minutes ago, and they had not gone far.
sentences.cn: 无论谁来过这儿都没超过十分钟离开，他们走不远。

socialize:2.en: Zero's first rule, according to the intercepted brief, was simple: never *socialize* with the targets. Keep distance, keep control. But the café log Ali had pulled showed Zero had met Grey Crow eleven times in the past month — same corner table, same hour. Zero had broken the rule. That meant Grey Crow was not just a guide. Grey Crow was leverage.
socialize:2.cnHint: 零点的规矩是绝不与目标____，但记录显示零点与灰鸦见面了十一次，这意味着灰鸦是人质筹码。
socialize:2.hook: My phone buzzed — a message from Grey Crow's number, but not Grey Crow's words.
socialize:2.line: 'I do not *socialize* with targets — yet here we both are.'

sentences.en: Zero's first rule, according to the intercepted brief, was simple: never *socialize* with the targets.
Keep distance, keep control.
sentences.cn: 保持距离，保持控制。

sentences.en: But the café log Ali had pulled showed Zero had met Grey Crow eleven times in the past month — same corner table, same hour.
sentences.cn: 但阿栗拉出来的咖啡馆日志显示零点在过去一个月里和灰鸦见过十一次——同一张角落桌，同一个时间。

sentences.en: Zero had broken the rule.
sentences.cn: 零点破了规则。

sentences.en: That meant Grey Crow was not just a guide.
sentences.cn: 那意味着灰鸦不只是个向导。

sentences.en: Grey Crow was leverage.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦是筹码。

lift:2.en: The old *lift* at the end of Block Nine had been out of service for a decade — or so the city records said. Tonight, its doors slid open on their own. Inside, a folded note waited on the floor. Someone had used it. Someone who knew I would come.
lift:2.cnHint: 九号楼尽头那部废弃的____突然自动开门，里面留着一张字条。
lift:2.hook: The number on the note matched a dead man's badge.
lift:2.line: 'Take the *lift* to floor zero — that floor does not exist on any map.'

sentences.en: The old *lift* at the end of Block Nine had been out of service for a decade — or so the city records said.
Tonight, its doors slid open on their own.
sentences.cn: 今晚，它的门自己滑开了。

sentences.en: Inside, a folded note waited on the floor.
sentences.cn: 里面，地板上等着一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: Someone had used it.
sentences.cn: 有人用过它。

sentences.en: Someone who knew I would come.
sentences.cn: 有人知道我会来。

mainly:2.en: The coded message was *mainly* numbers, but three letters near the end stood out: A-L-I. I read it twice in the cold light of the server room. Ali had not sent it — Ali was with me. Someone was using that name as a signal, or as a trap.
mainly:2.cnHint: 那条加密信息____是数字，但末尾有三个字母让调查员心跳加速。
mainly:2.hook: The timestamp on the message was one minute in the future.
mainly:2.line: 'The data is *mainly* clean, but those three letters — they were planted.'

sentences.en: The coded message was *mainly* numbers, but three letters near the end stood out: A-L-I.
I read it twice in the cold light of the server room.
sentences.cn: 我在服务器室的冷光下读了两遍。

sentences.en: Ali had not sent it — Ali was with me.
sentences.cn: 阿栗没有发它——阿栗和我在一起。

sentences.en: Someone was using that name as a signal, or as a trap.
sentences.cn: 有人用那个名字作为信号，或者作为陷阱。

nor:2.en: The package had no sender address, *nor* did it carry any signal tag I could read. Inside: one silver key and a strip of paper with four digits. Ali touched neither. I put on a glove and lifted the key to the scanner. The reader went dark.
nor:2.cnHint: 那个包裹没有发件人地址，也没有任何信号标签，里面只有一把钥匙和一串数字。
nor:2.hook: The scanner had never gone dark before — not once in six years.
nor:2.line: 'No name, *nor* any trace of a print — this was wiped clean by a professional.'

sentences.en: The package had no sender address, *nor* did it carry any signal tag I could read.
Inside: one silver key and a strip of paper with four digits.
sentences.cn: 里面：一把银钥匙和一张写着四个数字的纸条。

sentences.en: Ali touched neither.
sentences.cn: 阿栗什么都没碰。

sentences.en: I put on a glove and lifted the key to the scanner.
sentences.cn: 我戴上手套，把钥匙放到扫描仪上。

sentences.en: The reader went dark.
sentences.cn: 读取器黑屏了。

pick:2.en: Grey Crow told me to *pick* one file from the archive and burn the rest before dawn. Forty-seven files. I had ten minutes. Each name was a code, each code a door. I chose the one marked with a crow's feather drawn in red ink — and hoped I was right.
pick:2.cnHint: 引路人要求调查员在档案中____出一份，天亮前烧掉其余所有文件。
pick:2.hook: The moment I touched it, an alarm began counting down.
pick:2.line: '*Pick* carefully — the wrong file ends this for all of us.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow told me to *pick* one file from the archive and burn the rest before dawn.
Forty-seven files.
sentences.cn: 四十七份文件。

sentences.en: I had ten minutes.
sentences.cn: 我只有十分钟。

sentences.en: Each name was a code, each code a door.
sentences.cn: 每个名字都是密码，每个密码都是一扇门。

sentences.en: I chose the one marked with a crow's feather drawn in red ink — and hoped I was right.
sentences.cn: 我选了那份用红墨水画着乌鸦羽毛的——心里默祷自己没选错。

pollution:2.en: The harbor water glowed a dull orange — chemical *pollution* that had been creeping in for years. Hidden in the glow, a small metal case floated against the dock. Ali pulled it out. The lock was new. The case was not supposed to exist.
pollution:2.cnHint: 港口水面因____而发出暗橙色光芒，调查员和伙伴在其中发现了一个不该存在的金属箱。
pollution:2.hook: Inside, a voice chip began to play — Grey Crow's voice, recorded yesterday.
pollution:2.line: 'The *pollution* is not just in the water — it is in every signal this city sends.'

sentences.en: The harbor water glowed a dull orange — chemical *pollution* that had been creeping in for years.
Hidden in the glow, a small metal case floated against the dock.
sentences.cn: 隐在那暗淡的橘光里，一个小金属盒子贴着码头浮动。

sentences.en: Ali pulled it out.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把它拉了出来。

sentences.en: The lock was new.
sentences.cn: 锁是新的。

sentences.en: The case was not supposed to exist.
sentences.cn: 这个盒子本不该存在。

recall:2.en: I could not *recall* the exact words Grey Crow had used in our first meeting, but one phrase kept rising: 'the city forgets on purpose.' Now, holding a photo found behind a loose panel in the archive room, I understood what had been erased — and why.
recall:2.cnHint: 调查员努力____与引路人初次见面时的对话，一张从档案室夹缝中找到的照片让一切突然清晰。
recall:2.hook: The face in the photo was someone I had been told died ten years ago.
recall:2.line: '*Recall* every detail of that night — nothing was accidental, not even the silence.'

sentences.en: I could not *recall* the exact words Grey Crow had used in our first meeting, but one phrase kept rising: 'the city forgets on purpose.'
Now, holding a photo found behind a loose panel in the archive room, I understood what had been erased — and why.
sentences.cn: 现在，拿着从档案室松动的暗板后面找到的照片，我终于明白了什么被抹去了——以及为什么。

register:2.en: The old server room beneath the fish market smelled of rust and salt. I pressed my ID chip to the panel. The screen flickered: ACCESS DENIED. Grey Crow had warned me — to enter this grid, you had to *register* your voice pattern first, or the system locked you out for good.
register:2.cnHint: 我发现进入这个秘密服务器必须先将声纹____，否则系统永久封锁。
register:2.hook: The panel beeped once — then someone else's voice played back at me.
register:2.line: 'You must *register* your voice now, or this door stays shut forever.'

sentences.en: The old server room beneath the fish market smelled of rust and salt.
sentences.cn: 鱼市下面那间老服务器房闻起来都是铁锈和盐的味道。

sentences.en: I pressed my ID chip to the panel.
sentences.cn: 我把身份芯片贴到面板上。

sentences.en: The screen flickered: ACCESS DENIED.
sentences.cn: 屏幕闪烁：拒绝访问。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had warned me — to enter this grid, you had to *register* your voice pattern first, or the system locked you out for good.

skin:2.en: Ali slid the cracked data chip across the table. Under the blue lamp, I could see faint lines printed on it — a map, etched so small it looked like the pattern on human *skin*. Zero had hidden the coordinates in plain sight, pressed into the surface like a scar no one thought to read.
skin:2.cnHint: 芯片表面蚀刻的密纹细如____，零点把坐标就藏在那里。
skin:2.hook: The lines shifted under the light — the map was still changing.
skin:2.line: 'Look at it like *skin* — every line is a message, not a flaw.'

sentences.en: Ali slid the cracked data chip across the table.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把裂纹数据芯片推过桌子。

sentences.en: Under the blue lamp, I could see faint lines printed on it — a map, etched so small it looked like the pattern on human *skin*.
Zero had hidden the coordinates in plain sight, pressed into the surface like a scar no one thought to read.
sentences.cn: 零点把坐标藏在了众目睽睽之下，像疤痕一样按进表面，没人想过要读它。

spirit:2.en: The chapel at the edge of the port had been empty for thirty years. I found the message folded inside the hollow altar. Three words in Grey Crow's handwriting: HOLD YOUR *SPIRIT*. Around me, the walls hummed — this building was wired, every stone a microphone, every prayer a data packet.
spirit:2.cnHint: 礼拜堂里，引路人留下字条，叫我守住自己的____，而四壁都是窃听装置。
spirit:2.hook: The humming stopped — silence in Harbor City means only one thing.
spirit:2.line: 'Your *spirit* is the only thing Zero cannot hack — guard it.'

sentences.en: The chapel at the edge of the port had been empty for thirty years.
sentences.cn: 港口边缘的礼拜堂已经空了三十年。

sentences.en: I found the message folded inside the hollow altar.
sentences.cn: 我在中空的祭坛里找到了那张纸条。

sentences.en: Three words in Grey Crow's handwriting: HOLD YOUR *SPIRIT*.
Around me, the walls hummed — this building was wired, every stone a microphone, every prayer a data packet.
sentences.cn: 四周，墙壁嗡嗡作响——这座建筑被装满了线路，每块石头都是麦克风，每次祈祷都是一个数据包。

spread:2.en: I climbed to the roof of the old print house. Below, neon light *spread* across the wet streets like spilled paint, block after block, all the way to the dark water. Somewhere in that glow, Zero's signal was moving — Ali's tracker showed a red dot, slow and steady, heading for the bridge.
spread:2.cnHint: 霓虹光芒向远处____开去，零点的信号正缓缓移向大桥。
spread:2.hook: The red dot stopped — right at the center of the bridge.
spread:2.line: 'Watch how the light *spreads* — Zero always moves where the crowd is thickest.'

sentences.en: I climbed to the roof of the old print house.
sentences.cn: 我爬上了老印刷厂的屋顶。

sentences.en: Below, neon light *spread* across the wet streets like spilled paint, block after block, all the way to the dark water.
Somewhere in that glow, Zero's signal was moving — Ali's tracker showed a red dot, slow and steady, heading for the bridge.
sentences.cn: 在那片光芒里的某处，零点的信号在移动——阿栗的追踪器显示一个红点，缓慢而稳定地朝桥靠近。

totally:2.en: The file Grey Crow had sent me was *totally* blank — no text, no image, nothing but white. I almost closed it. Then Ali leaned in and held a black-light pen over the screen. Letters appeared, row after row, burning green in the dark: a list of names, and mine was last.
totally:2.cnHint: 文件看起来____是空白，直到阿栗用特殊光照出了隐藏的名单。
totally:2.hook: My name on the list had a single red mark beside it.
totally:2.line: 'The file is *totally* clean on the surface — that is exactly the problem.'

sentences.en: The file Grey Crow had sent me was *totally* blank — no text, no image, nothing but white.
I almost closed it.
sentences.cn: 我差点关掉它。

sentences.en: Then Ali leaned in and held a black-light pen over the screen.
sentences.cn: 然后阿栗靠过来，用黑光笔在屏幕上照了一下。

sentences.en: Letters appeared, row after row, burning green in the dark: a list of names, and mine was last.
sentences.cn: 字母出现了，一行行，在黑暗中烧出绿光：一份名单，我的名字在最后。

tree:2.en: The meet point was a dead *tree* in the flooded park, its bark carved with old gang signs. I found a hollow at the root. Inside: a small metal box, still warm, as if someone had placed it there seconds ago. The box had no lock. It had a heartbeat sensor instead.
tree:2.cnHint: 枯____根部的藏物盒刚刚被人放入，它用心跳感应代替锁。
tree:2.hook: My pulse was too fast — the sensor flashed red and started counting down.
tree:2.line: 'Meet me at the dead *tree* — and keep your heartbeat steady when you arrive.'

sentences.en: The meet point was a dead *tree* in the flooded park, its bark carved with old gang signs.
I found a hollow at the root.
sentences.cn: 我在树根的凹陷处找到了一个小金属盒。

sentences.en: Inside: a small metal box, still warm, as if someone had placed it there seconds ago.
sentences.cn: 里面：一个小金属盒子，还温热着，好像有人几秒前才放进去的。

sentences.en: The box had no lock.
sentences.cn: 盒子没有锁。

sentences.en: It had a heartbeat sensor instead.
sentences.cn: 反而有一个心跳传感器。

weigh:2.en: Grey Crow's last note gave me two choices: hand the chip to the city council, or destroy it and let Zero walk free. I sat in the cold stairwell and tried to *weigh* each option against the other. The chip held enough truth to end careers — or start a war. Neither path felt clean.
weigh:2.cnHint: 我在楼道里____两个选项，每一个代价都沉重得难以承受。
weigh:2.hook: A door opened above me — someone had been listening the whole time.
weigh:2.line: 'You have to *weigh* what one truth is worth against what it will cost.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow's last note gave me two choices: hand the chip to the city council, or destroy it and let Zero walk free.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦的最后一张纸条给了我两个选择：把芯片交给市议会，或者销毁它，让零点逃脱。

sentences.en: I sat in the cold stairwell and tried to *weigh* each option against the other.
The chip held enough truth to end careers — or start a war.
sentences.cn: 芯片里的真相足以毁掉生涯——或者引发战争。

sentences.en: Neither path felt clean.
sentences.cn: 两条路都不干净。

alive:2.en: The signal went dead at 03:00. Ali checked the relay box; I checked the wire. Then we heard it — a single tone, steady and low, pushing through the noise. Grey Crow was still *alive*, still transmitting, using a frequency so old the city's scanners did not even look for it anymore.
alive:2.cnHint: 微弱的旧频率信号证明引路人依然____，并仍在传送消息。
alive:2.hook: The tone carried six words — and the sixth word was my name.
alive:2.line: 'As long as that tone holds, Grey Crow is *alive* — do not touch the dial.'

sentences.en: The signal went dead at 03:00.
sentences.cn: 信号在03:00断了。

sentences.en: Ali checked the relay box; I checked the wire.
sentences.cn: 阿栗检查了中继盒；我检查了电线。

sentences.en: Then we heard it — a single tone, steady and low, pushing through the noise.
sentences.cn: 然后我们听到了——一声单独的音调，稳定而低沉，穿过噪声传来。

sentences.en: Grey Crow was still *alive*, still transmitting, using a frequency so old the city's scanners did not even look for it anymore.

anyway:2.en: The message was short, burned into a strip of paper left under a broken lamp in the old port district. I had been told to stay back. But the signal was already in my head, pulling me forward. I went *anyway*, stepping over cracked stone into the dark water smell of the docks.
anyway:2.cnHint: 调查员无视警告，____前往港区寻找那张纸条留下的线索。
anyway:2.hook: The paper dissolved in my hand, but the code stayed behind my eyes.
anyway:2.line: '*Anyway*, the message led here — and here is where the truth hides.'

sentences.en: The message was short, burned into a strip of paper left under a broken lamp in the old port district.
sentences.cn: 信息很短，烧刻在旧港区一盏破灯下留下的纸条上。

sentences.en: I had been told to stay back.
sentences.cn: 我被告诫要留在后面。

sentences.en: But the signal was already in my head, pulling me forward.
sentences.cn: 但信号已经在我脑子里了，把我往前拉。

sentences.en: I went *anyway*, stepping over cracked stone into the dark water smell of the docks.

arise:2.en: Grey Crow had warned me: new dangers *arise* when old codes are broken. I found the proof in a locked storage room beneath the market — rows of blank signal tags, each one wiped clean, waiting to carry forbidden words again. Someone had been preparing this for a long time.
arise:2.cnHint: 调查员在市场地下仓库发现了空白信号标签，印证了灰鸦所说的危险会____的警告。
arise:2.hook: One tag still held a half-deleted word I almost recognised.
arise:2.line: 'Problems *arise* fast when you open a channel that was meant to stay shut.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow had warned me: new dangers *arise* when old codes are broken.
I found the proof in a locked storage room beneath the market — rows of blank signal tags, each one wiped clean, waiting to carry forbidden words again.
sentences.cn: 我在市集下面的一间上了锁的储藏室里找到了证据——一排排空白的信号标签，每一个都被清空了，等着重新承载禁忌的词汇。

sentences.en: Someone had been preparing this for a long time.
sentences.cn: 有人为这一切准备了很久。

besides:2.en: Ali pressed the small metal box into my hands. 'It holds the counter-code,' she said. *Besides* the code itself, the box carried a faint warmth — her fingers had held it a long time before giving it up. I understood then what it had cost her to hand it over at all.
besides:2.cnHint: 阿栗将金属盒交给调查员，盒子里____有反制码，还带着她手心残留的温度。
besides:2.hook: But the box had already begun to hum, counting down to something.
besides:2.line: '*Besides* the code, there is one more thing inside — do not open it alone.'

sentences.en: Ali pressed the small metal box into my hands.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把一个小金属盒按进我的手心。

sentences.en: 'It holds the counter-code,' she said.
sentences.cn: "里面装着反制密码，"她说。

sentences.en: *Besides* the code itself, the box carried a faint warmth — her fingers had held it a long time before giving it up.
I understood then what it had cost her to hand it over at all.
sentences.cn: 我这才明白，她能把它交出来，本身就是多大的代价。

certainly:2.en: The drop point was a cracked wall near the east bridge, covered in layered graffiti. Grey Crow had *certainly* been here — I could read the pattern, three marks and a gap, his sign. But the marks were fresh, and the bridge gate stood open. He had left only minutes ago, or someone wanted me to think so.
certainly:2.cnHint: 调查员在东桥附近的涂鸦墙上发现灰鸦的标记，____是他留下的，但情况似乎有些不对。
certainly:2.hook: Behind the last layer of paint, a different hand had left a second message.
certainly:2.line: 'He was *certainly* here — the sign is his, but the timing is wrong.'

sentences.en: The drop point was a cracked wall near the east bridge, covered in layered graffiti.
sentences.cn: 接头点是东桥附近一面裂开的墙，上面层层叠叠贴满了涂鸦。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had *certainly* been here — I could read the pattern, three marks and a gap, his sign.
But the marks were fresh, and the bridge gate stood open.
sentences.cn: 但这些记号很新鲜，桥门也开着。

sentences.en: He had left only minutes ago, or someone wanted me to think so.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦几分钟前才离开过，要么就是有人想让我这么想。

challenging:2.en: Decoding Zero's broadcast was *challenging* in a way no training had prepared me for. The signal shifted layer by layer, each layer using a different rule. I cracked the first three, then stopped cold. The fourth layer was not a code. It was a question — and it was addressed to me by name.
challenging:2.cnHint: 调查员发现解码零点的广播极具____性，第四层竟然是一个直接写着自己名字的问题。
challenging:2.hook: I had never told Zero my name.
challenging:2.line: 'This level is *challenging* — Zero built it to stop anyone who got this far.'

sentences.en: Decoding Zero's broadcast was *challenging* in a way no training had prepared me for.
The signal shifted layer by layer, each layer using a different rule.
sentences.cn: 信号一层层变换，每一层都用不同的规则。

sentences.en: I cracked the first three, then stopped cold.
sentences.cn: 前三层我都破解了，然后就停住了。

sentences.en: The fourth layer was not a code.
sentences.cn: 第四层不是密码。

sentences.en: It was a question — and it was addressed to me by name.
sentences.cn: 是一个问题——用我的名字直接问我。

circumstance:2.en: Under normal *circumstance* I would have waited for orders. But the signal flooding my mind was urgent, a sharp tone like a fire alarm no one else could hear. I found the object on my own: a glass chip no bigger than a fingernail, taped inside a hollow step at the base of the signal tower.
circumstance:2.cnHint: 在特殊____下，调查员独自在信号塔底部台阶里找到了一块指甲盖大小的玻璃芯片。
circumstance:2.hook: The chip began to glow the moment my skin touched it.
circumstance:2.line: 'Given the *circumstance*, I acted alone — I hope that was the right call.'

sentences.en: Under normal *circumstance* I would have waited for orders.
But the signal flooding my mind was urgent, a sharp tone like a fire alarm no one else could hear.
sentences.cn: 但冲进我脑子里的信号很急促，像一声只有我能听到的火警警报。

sentences.en: I found the object on my own: a glass chip no bigger than a fingernail, taped inside a hollow step at the base of the signal tower.
sentences.cn: 我自己找到了那个东西：一片玻璃芯片，指甲大小，用胶带粘在信号塔底部一个中空的台阶里面。

comfort:2.en: Ali found me sitting on the cold floor of the relay station, the glass chip still warm in my palm. She said nothing at first. The *comfort* in her silence was real — no forced words, just the sound of rain on the roof and two people thinking hard about the same problem.
comfort:2.cnHint: 阿栗在中继站找到调查员，她沉默带来的____让调查员平静下来，两人一起面对眼前的谜题。
comfort:2.hook: Then her eyes dropped to the chip and her face went completely still.
comfort:2.line: 'I cannot give you answers, but I can give you *comfort* — you read the signs right.'

sentences.en: Ali found me sitting on the cold floor of the relay station, the glass chip still warm in my palm.
sentences.cn: 阿栗发现我坐在中继站冰冷的地板上，那片玻璃芯片还温热地躺在我的手心。

sentences.en: She said nothing at first.
sentences.cn: 她开始什么都没说。

sentences.en: The *comfort* in her silence was real — no forced words, just the sound of rain on the roof and two people thinking hard about the same problem.

enrich:2.en: Grey Crow had spent years helping people *enrich* their private languages — small coded phrases that the city's filters could not catch. I found his record in the hidden archive: hundreds of names, hundreds of small rebellions made from words. My name was not there. But Ali's was, near the top.
enrich:2.cnHint: 调查员在隐藏档案中发现灰鸦帮助许多人____他们的私密语言，阿栗的名字赫然在列。
enrich:2.hook: Ali had never once mentioned knowing Grey Crow before today.
enrich:2.line: 'He used language to *enrich* lives — every code he taught was a small act of freedom.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow had spent years helping people *enrich* their private languages — small coded phrases that the city's filters could not catch.
I found his record in the hidden archive: hundreds of names, hundreds of small rebellions made from words.
sentences.cn: 我在隐藏的档案库里找到了他的记录：数百个名字，数百场用词语制造的小小反抗。

sentences.en: My name was not there.
sentences.cn: 我的名字不在里面。

sentences.en: But Ali's was, near the top.
sentences.cn: 但阿栗的在，靠近最前面。

egg:2.en: The sealed room smelled of old paper and burnt wire. On the desk sat a small clay *egg*, its surface carved with micro-glyphs I had never seen before. Ali said Zero used these to store forbidden code — crack it wrong and everything inside would erase. My hands would not stop shaking.
egg:2.cnHint: 调查员在密室里发现了一枚刻有神秘符文的____，据说里面藏着被禁止的代码。
egg:2.hook: One wrong move and the truth inside vanishes forever.
egg:2.line: 'That *egg* holds the last copy of Zero\'s master key.'

sentences.en: The sealed room smelled of old paper and burnt wire.
sentences.cn: 密闭的房间闻起来有陈纸和烧焦电线的味道。

sentences.en: On the desk sat a small clay *egg*, its surface carved with micro-glyphs I had never seen before.
Ali said Zero used these to store forbidden code — crack it wrong and everything inside would erase.
sentences.cn: 阿栗说零点用这些来存储禁忌密码——破解错了整个东西就会自动擦除。

sentences.en: My hands would not stop shaking.
sentences.cn: 我的手开始不停地发抖。

hire:2.en: Grey Crow slid a thin card across the wet table. 'Consider this your formal *hire*,' he said, voice flat as the rain outside. I stared at the number printed on it — three zeros too many for a rookie. Ali warned me once: when the pay is too high, the job is too dangerous. I picked up the card anyway.
hire:2.cnHint: 引路人递给调查员一张____通知书，上面的报酬高得反常。
hire:2.hook: Nobody pays that much unless they expect you not to come back.
hire:2.line: 'Your *hire* starts now — and so does the risk.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow slid a thin card across the wet table.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦把一张薄卡片推过湿漉漉的桌子。

sentences.en: 'Consider this your formal *hire*,' he said, voice flat as the rain outside.
I stared at the number printed on it — three zeros too many for a rookie.
sentences.cn: 我盯着上面印的数字——对于一个新手来说多了三个零。

sentences.en: Ali warned me once: when the pay is too high, the job is too dangerous.
sentences.cn: 阿栗曾经警告过我：报酬太高的时候，工作就太危险了。

sentences.en: I picked up the card anyway.
sentences.cn: 我还是拿起了那张卡片。

aid:2.en: The broadcast tower on Pier Nine was dark. I found Ali crouched behind a relay box, pressing a torn cloth to her wrist. 'I\'m fine,' she said, but she was not. I used the only *aid* kit in my bag — three strips of tape and a cooling patch — and hoped it would be enough to get us both out.
aid:2.cnHint: 调查员在码头铁塔旁找到受伤的阿栗，用仅有的____包扎了伤口。
aid:2.hook: Outside, Zero\'s signal was getting closer by the second.
aid:2.line: 'This *aid* kit is the last thing standing between us and real trouble.'

sentences.en: The broadcast tower on Pier Nine was dark.
sentences.cn: 九号码头的广播塔一片黑暗。

sentences.en: I found Ali crouched behind a relay box, pressing a torn cloth to her wrist.
sentences.cn: 我发现阿栗蹲在一个中继盒后面，用破布按着她的手腕。

sentences.en: 'I\'m fine,' she said, but she was not.
sentences.cn: "我没事，"她说，但其实不是。

sentences.en: I used the only *aid* kit in my bag — three strips of tape and a cooling patch — and hoped it would be enough to get us both out.

bill:2.en: Tucked behind a cracked wall panel in Sub-Level Four, I found a single paper *bill* — old currency, long worthless — but someone had printed a sixteen-digit cipher along its edge in UV ink. Grey Crow once told me Zero never used data files. He preferred things you could burn. This could not be burned yet.
bill:2.cnHint: 调查员在地下四层的夹墙里发现了一张纸质____，边缘用紫外线墨水印着密码。
bill:2.hook: Whoever left it here was either very careful — or very dead.
bill:2.line: 'That *bill* isn\'t money — it\'s the only map that matters.'

sentences.en: Tucked behind a cracked wall panel in Sub-Level Four, I found a single paper *bill* — old currency, long worthless — but someone had printed a sixteen-digit cipher along its edge in UV ink.
Grey Crow once told me Zero never used data files.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦曾经跟我说过零点从不用数据文件。

sentences.en: He preferred things you could burn.
sentences.cn: 他喜欢能烧掉的东西。

sentences.en: This could not be burned yet.
sentences.cn: 这个还烧不了。

paint:2.en: The message was hidden in plain view. Someone had used red *paint* on the underside of the harbor bridge to write forty characters that looked like street art. But when I tilted my decoder lens, the pattern collapsed into coordinates and a single name: Zero. Ali grabbed my arm. We had been standing here too long.
paint:2.cnHint: 调查员用解码镜透视桥底的____涂鸦，发现了隐藏的坐标和一个名字。
paint:2.hook: The paint was still wet — whoever wrote it had just left.
paint:2.line: 'Read the *paint* fast — this message has an expiry time.'

sentences.en: The message was hidden in plain view.
sentences.cn: 信息就藏在众目睽睽之下。

sentences.en: Someone had used red *paint* on the underside of the harbor bridge to write forty characters that looked like street art.
But when I tilted my decoder lens, the pattern collapsed into coordinates and a single name: Zero.
sentences.cn: 但当我转动解码镜头时，图案一下子塌陷成坐标和一个名字：零点。

sentences.en: Ali grabbed my arm.
sentences.cn: 阿栗抓住我的手臂。

sentences.en: We had been standing here too long.
sentences.cn: 我们在这里站得太久了。

bean:2.en: Grey Crow left me a cold cup on the window ledge of the safe house — one coffee *bean* resting on the lid, which was his signal for danger nearby. I had not seen him use it in two years. I killed the lights, pulled the blinds, and listened. Footsteps in the corridor. Two pairs, moving slow.
bean:2.cnHint: 引路人在安全屋窗台留下一颗咖啡____作为暗号，示意附近有危险。
bean:2.hook: The footsteps stopped — right outside my door.
bean:2.line: 'One *bean* on the lid means run — two means it\'s already too late.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow left me a cold cup on the window ledge of the safe house — one coffee *bean* resting on the lid, which was his signal for danger nearby.
I had not seen him use it in two years.
sentences.cn: 两年来我没见他用过这个信号。

sentences.en: I killed the lights, pulled the blinds, and listened.
sentences.cn: 我关掉了灯，拉下百叶窗，竖起耳朵听。

sentences.en: Footsteps in the corridor.
sentences.cn: 走廊里有脚步声。

sentences.en: Two pairs, moving slow.
sentences.cn: 两对脚，走得很慢。

birthday:2.en: The encrypted file was named after a date — today\'s date. My *birthday*. I had never told anyone in Harbor City when I was born. Grey Crow swore he did not send it. Ali went pale when she read the header. Someone inside our own network had been watching me long before I started watching them.
birthday:2.cnHint: 一份以调查员____命名的加密文件突然出现，没有人承认发送过它。
birthday:2.hook: Only the enemy knew that date — which meant the enemy was very close.
birthday:2.line: 'Using your *birthday* as a filename — that\'s not a coincidence, it\'s a threat.'

sentences.en: The encrypted file was named after a date — today\'s date.
sentences.cn: 加密文件是用一个日期命名的——今天的日期。

sentences.en: My *birthday*.
I had never told anyone in Harbor City when I was born.
sentences.cn: 我从没告诉港市的任何人我的出生日期。

sentences.en: Grey Crow swore he did not send it.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦发誓说不是他发的。

sentences.en: Ali went pale when she read the header.
sentences.cn: 阿栗读到文件头时脸色苍白。

sentences.en: Someone inside our own network had been watching me long before I started watching them.
sentences.cn: 我们自己网络内部有人早就开始监视我了，远在我开始监视他们之前。

flight:2.en: Gate Seven at the mag-rail hub showed one last *flight* departing for the outer grid at midnight. Pinned to the seat map on the public board was a folded note in Grey Crow\'s handwriting: two words — 'Don\'t board.' I checked the passenger list. Zero\'s alias was in seat four. So was mine.
flight:2.cnHint: 调查员在磁轨站看到午夜____的乘客名单，发现自己的名字和对手的别名同时出现。
flight:2.hook: Someone had booked us both on the same one-way trip.
flight:2.line: 'Cancel that *flight* — or we both disappear off the grid tonight.'

sentences.en: Gate Seven at the mag-rail hub showed one last *flight* departing for the outer grid at midnight.
Pinned to the seat map on the public board was a folded note in Grey Crow\'s handwriting: two words — 'Don\'t board.'
sentences.cn: 钉在公告板上的座位图旁边，是灰鸦笔迹的一张折起来的纸条：两个字——"别上车"。

sentences.en: I checked the passenger list.
sentences.cn: 我查了乘客名单。

sentences.en: Zero\'s alias was in seat four.
sentences.cn: 零点的化名在第四座。

sentences.en: So was mine.
sentences.cn: 我的也在。

facilitate:2.en: Ali slid a small data chip across the wet table. 'Grey Crow left this,' she said. The chip held a routing map — every back-channel tunnel in the old port district. It was designed to *facilitate* our movement through Zero's signal blocks, turning a locked city into an open road. I pocketed it without a word.
facilitate:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给我一块芯片，它能____我们穿越零点的信号封锁区。
facilitate:2.hook: But the chip was already warm — someone had read it before us.
facilitate:2.line: 'This map will *facilitate* your path through Zero's net.'

sentences.en: Ali slid a small data chip across the wet table.
sentences.cn: 阿栗把一张小数据芯片推过湿漉漉的桌子。

sentences.en: 'Grey Crow left this,' she said.
sentences.cn: "灰鸦留下的，"她说。

sentences.en: The chip held a routing map — every back-channel tunnel in the old port district.
sentences.cn: 芯片里存着一张路由图——老港区每一条暗道隧道。

sentences.en: It was designed to *facilitate* our movement through Zero's signal blocks, turning a locked city into an open road.
I pocketed it without a word.
sentences.cn: 我无言地把它装进了口袋。

insight:2.en: The message was burned into the wall of a flooded parking deck: forty-seven symbols, each one a dead frequency. I stared until my eyes ached. Then one pattern clicked. That single *insight* rewrote everything — Zero was not blocking the signal. Zero was the signal. The city itself was broadcasting his code.
insight:2.cnHint: 我盯着墙上的密文，突然获得____，发现零点才是信号本身。
insight:2.hook: If Zero was the signal, then every screen in Harbor City was his eye.
insight:2.line: 'One moment of *insight* and the whole case flips upside down.'

sentences.en: The message was burned into the wall of a flooded parking deck: forty-seven symbols, each one a dead frequency.
sentences.cn: 信息被烧刻在一个被水淹没的停车场的墙上：四十七个符号，每一个都是一个死频率。

sentences.en: I stared until my eyes ached.
sentences.cn: 我盯着看，直到眼睛酸疼。

sentences.en: Then one pattern clicked.
sentences.cn: 然后一个图案突然咔哒一声对上了。

sentences.en: That single *insight* rewrote everything — Zero was not blocking the signal.
Zero was the signal.
sentences.cn: 零点就是信号。

sentences.en: The city itself was broadcasting his code.
sentences.cn: 整座城市都在广播他的代码。

preparation:2.en: Grey Crow's safe-room was a mess of printed maps, cold coffee, and clipped wire. Ali touched a stack of coded notes. 'This is months of *preparation*,' she said quietly. Every move Zero might make was already marked in red. Whoever Grey Crow feared, they had feared them for a long time.
preparation:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的密室里堆满了资料，那是数月____的成果，令阿栗沉默。
preparation:2.hook: Then Ali turned over the last page and her face went pale.
preparation:2.line: 'Months of *preparation*, and still no guaranteed way out.'

sentences.en: Grey Crow's safe-room was a mess of printed maps, cold coffee, and clipped wire.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦的安全屋是一片混乱——印刷地图、冷咖啡和剪断的电线。

sentences.en: Ali touched a stack of coded notes.
sentences.cn: 阿栗摸了摸一沓编码便签。

sentences.en: 'This is months of *preparation*,' she said quietly.
Every move Zero might make was already marked in red.
sentences.cn: 零点可能做出的每一步都用红色标记了。

sentences.en: Whoever Grey Crow feared, they had feared them for a long time.
sentences.cn: 不管灰鸦害怕谁，他早就开始害怕他们了。

separate:2.en: Zero's broadcast split mid-signal — two identical streams sent to two *separate* towers on opposite ends of Harbor City. It was a classic split-echo trick: force us to divide. Ali looked at me. I looked at the map. We had one minute to choose, and only one of us could be right.
separate:2.cnHint: 零点将信号分成两路，发往两个____的信号塔，逼我们分兵。
separate:2.hook: The clock hit zero and we still hadn't moved.
separate:2.line: 'He sent them to two *separate* towers — he wants us split.'

sentences.en: Zero's broadcast split mid-signal — two identical streams sent to two *separate* towers on opposite ends of Harbor City.
It was a classic split-echo trick: force us to divide.
sentences.cn: 这是一个经典的分流回声把戏：逼迫我们分散。

sentences.en: Ali looked at me.
sentences.cn: 阿栗看着我。

sentences.en: I looked at the map.
sentences.cn: 我看着地图。

sentences.en: We had one minute to choose, and only one of us could be right.
sentences.cn: 我们只有一分钟来选择，而且只有我们中的一个能是对的。

tie:2.en: The evidence board showed a clean *tie*: every lead pointing to Zero was matched by a lead pointing somewhere else. Nothing won. Nothing lost. Ali called it beautiful. I called it a trap. Someone had spent real effort making sure we could never be certain — and that someone knew exactly how we think.
tie:2.cnHint: 证据板上两条线索打成____，阿栗说这很美，我说这是陷阱。
tie:2.hook: A perfect tie in an investigation means someone built it that way.
tie:2.line: 'It's a *tie* — and a tie here means Zero planned every step.'

sentences.en: The evidence board showed a clean *tie*: every lead pointing to Zero was matched by a lead pointing somewhere else.
Nothing won.
sentences.cn: 什么都没赢。

sentences.en: Nothing lost.
sentences.cn: 什么都没输。

sentences.en: Ali called it beautiful.
sentences.cn: 阿栗说这很美。

sentences.en: I called it a trap.
sentences.cn: 我说这是个陷阱。

sentences.en: Someone had spent real effort making sure we could never be certain — and that someone knew exactly how we think.
sentences.cn: 有人费了大力气确保我们永远无法确定——而那个人完全知道我们怎么想。

jam:2.en: I found the note inside a cracked public phone near the old fish market. The paper read: 'At noon, listen.' At noon, every city channel hit a solid *jam* — pure noise, ear-splitting static. But under the noise, one clean voice counting down from ten. Grey Crow's voice. I pressed my back to the wall and listened hard.
jam:2.cnHint: 正午时分所有频道遭到____，但噪音之下隐藏着灰鸦的倒计时声音。
jam:2.hook: The countdown stopped at three — and then went silent forever.
jam:2.line: 'The *jam* covers the whole band — except the one frequency that matters.'

sentences.en: I found the note inside a cracked public phone near the old fish market.
sentences.cn: 我在老鱼市场附近的一个裂开的公用电话里找到了纸条。

sentences.en: The paper read: 'At noon, listen.'
sentences.cn: 纸上写着："正午时，听。"

sentences.en: At noon, every city channel hit a solid *jam* — pure noise, ear-splitting static.
But under the noise, one clean voice counting down from ten.
sentences.cn: 但在噪声下面，一个清晰的声音在倒数——从十开始。

sentences.en: Grey Crow's voice.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦的声音。

sentences.en: I pressed my back to the wall and listened hard.
sentences.cn: 我把背靠在墙上，竖起耳朵仔细听。

supermarket:2.en: The meet point was the top floor of a flooded *supermarket* in Block Nine — shelves still full of rusting cans, signs still lit in dead pink neon. Ali got there first. She found a folded sheet between two cans: a list of names, all of them investigators, all of them marked with a small red dot. My name was third.
supermarket:2.cnHint: 约定地点是一家废弃____的顶层，阿栗在那里发现了一份名单，我的名字在上面。
supermarket:2.hook: I counted the red dots — and realised one name had two.
supermarket:2.line: 'Meet me at the old *supermarket* on Block Nine — top floor, come alone.'

sentences.en: The meet point was the top floor of a flooded *supermarket* in Block Nine — shelves still full of rusting cans, signs still lit in dead pink neon.
Ali got there first.
sentences.cn: 阿栗先到了。

sentences.en: She found a folded sheet between two cans: a list of names, all of them investigators, all of them marked with a small red dot.
sentences.cn: 她在两罐罐头之间找到了一张折起来的纸：一份名单，都是调查员，都用一个小红点标记了。

sentences.en: My name was third.
sentences.cn: 我的名字排第三。

debate:2.en: Ali and I stood over the decoded file and *debated* for three cold minutes. She said the drop point was the north bridge. I said it was the east tunnel. Neither of us moved. Then Grey Crow's voice cut through the ear-piece: 'Stop talking. Zero already knows which one you'll choose.' The line went dead.
debate:2.cnHint: 阿栗和我就接头地点____了三分钟，而灰鸦警告零点早已知道答案。
debate:2.hook: If Zero knew our choice before we made it, the trap was already closed.
debate:2.line: 'We can *debate* all night — Zero won't wait for us to agree.'

sentences.en: Ali and I stood over the decoded file and *debated* for three cold minutes.
She said the drop point was the north bridge.
sentences.cn: 她说投递地点是北桥。

sentences.en: I said it was the east tunnel.
sentences.cn: 我说是东隧道。

sentences.en: Neither of us moved.
sentences.cn: 我们都没动。

sentences.en: Then Grey Crow's voice cut through the ear-piece: 'Stop talking.
sentences.cn: 然后灰鸦的声音切进了耳机："停止说话。

sentences.en: Zero already knows which one you'll choose.'
sentences.cn: 零点已经知道你们会选哪个了。"

sentences.en: The line went dead.
sentences.cn: 线路断了。

housing:2.en: The coded signal led me to a forgotten block on the east side. Every wall was covered in cipher graffiti. Grey Crow had marked the *housing* records office — a grey building with barred windows. 'Old data lives here,' he had warned me. Inside, one file glowed on a dead screen.
housing:2.cnHint: 我追踪信号来到一栋旧楼，灰鸦说这里的____档案里藏着秘密。
housing:2.hook: The file had my name on it.
housing:2.line: 'The *housing* records hold every name they tried to erase,' Grey Crow said.

sentences.en: The coded signal led me to a forgotten block on the east side.
sentences.cn: 编码信号把我引到了东边的一个被遗忘的街区。

sentences.en: Every wall was covered in cipher graffiti.
sentences.cn: 每堵墙都覆盖了密码涂鸦。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had marked the *housing* records office — a grey building with barred windows.
'Old data lives here,' he had warned me.
sentences.cn: "老数据住在这里，"他曾警告我。

sentences.en: Inside, one file glowed on a dead screen.
sentences.cn: 屋里，一个文件在死屏上闪闪发光。

behaviour:2.en: I watched Zero from across the rain-slicked plaza. His *behaviour* was off — too slow, too careful, like a man who knew he was being read. Ali pressed close and whispered that Zero had changed his whole pattern in the last hour. Something had spooked him.
behaviour:2.cnHint: 我注意到零点的____很反常，阿栗说他最近一小时改变了所有行动规律。
behaviour:2.hook: Then Zero looked straight at me through the neon haze.
behaviour:2.line: 'His *behaviour* tells me he already knows we are here,' Ali said.

sentences.en: I watched Zero from across the rain-slicked plaza.
sentences.cn: 我隔着雨水闪闪发亮的广场注视着零点。

sentences.en: His *behaviour* was off — too slow, too careful, like a man who knew he was being read.
Ali pressed close and whispered that Zero had changed his whole pattern in the last hour.
sentences.cn: 阿栗贴近我耳边，低声说零点在过去一小时内彻底改变了他的行动模式。

sentences.en: Something had spooked him.
sentences.cn: 什么东西吓到了他。

husband:2.en: The message was sealed inside a cracked wall panel near the old market. It was addressed to a woman named only 'R.' The sender called himself her *husband*, though the city had no record of that bond. Ali read it twice and went quiet.
husband:2.cnHint: 那封藏在墙缝里的信来自一个自称 R 的____的人，但城市档案里没有任何记录。
husband:2.hook: Ali's hand was shaking when she folded the letter.
husband:2.line: 'He signed it: your *husband*, always,' Ali said softly.

sentences.en: The message was sealed inside a cracked wall panel near the old market.
sentences.cn: 那条信息被封在旧市场附近一块裂开的墙板里。

sentences.en: It was addressed to a woman named only 'R.'
sentences.cn: 信上只署了一个女人的名字——"R"。

sentences.en: The sender called himself her *husband*, though the city had no record of that bond.
Ali read it twice and went quiet.
sentences.cn: 阿栗读了两遍，沉默了。

tourist:2.en: I dressed in a bright coat and moved through the night market like a *tourist*, wide-eyed and slow. Zero's people never look twice at lost visitors. Grey Crow had taught me that trick. Under a noodle stall, I found the data chip taped to the bench.
tourist:2.cnHint: 我伪装成____混入夜市，在一个摊位下找到了藏好的数据芯片。
tourist:2.line: 'Walk like a *tourist* — they will never see the hunter in you,' Grey Crow told me.

sentences.en: I dressed in a bright coat and moved through the night market like a *tourist*, wide-eyed and slow.
Zero's people never look twice at lost visitors.
sentences.cn: 零点的人从来不会多看迷路的游客一眼。

sentences.en: Grey Crow had taught me that trick.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦教过我这一招。

sentences.en: Under a noodle stall, I found the data chip taped to the bench.
sentences.cn: 在一个面摊下面，我找到了用胶带粘在长凳上的数据芯片。

agent:2.en: The sealed door at the end of the corridor had one word burned into its surface: ZERO. Ali checked the lock and froze. She said the room had last been opened by an *agent* of the city council — someone with clearance far above ours. A cold hum came from inside.
agent:2.cnHint: 走廊尽头的房间上次是由某个____打开的，级别远高于我们，里面传来低沉的嗡嗡声。
agent:2.hook: The lock clicked open on its own.
agent:2.line: 'Only an *agent* of the council could have sealed it this tight,' Ali said.

sentences.en: The sealed door at the end of the corridor had one word burned into its surface: ZERO.
sentences.cn: 走廊尽头的那扇密封门上烧进了一个单词：零点。

sentences.en: Ali checked the lock and froze.
sentences.cn: 阿栗检查了锁，僵住了。

sentences.en: She said the room had last been opened by an *agent* of the city council — someone with clearance far above ours.
A cold hum came from inside.
sentences.cn: 里面传来一阵冷冰冰的嗡鸣声。

cash:2.en: Grey Crow left me a small box behind the signal tower. Inside was a folded note and a stack of old paper *cash* — the kind nobody had used in forty years. The note said: 'They still trade in this below the city. Go down. Ask for the map.'
cash:2.cnHint: 灰鸦留给我一盒四十年没人用过的纸质____，纸条上说城市地下还有人用它做交易。
cash:2.hook: Below the last line, a second hand had written: 'Do not trust the map.'
cash:2.line: 'Paper *cash* is the only thing their sensors cannot track,' Grey Crow had written.

sentences.en: Grey Crow left me a small box behind the signal tower.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦在信号塔后留给我一个小盒子。

sentences.en: Inside was a folded note and a stack of old paper *cash* — the kind nobody had used in forty years.
The note said: 'They still trade in this below the city.
sentences.cn: 纸条上写着："他们还在城市下面用这种东西交易。

sentences.en: Go down.
sentences.cn: 往下去。

sentences.en: Ask for the map.'
sentences.cn: 问他们要地图。"

competition:2.en: Zero had posted a public *competition* on the city grid — a code-breaking contest, open to all. Ali said it was a trap to pull every skilled hacker into the open. Grey Crow agreed. But buried in the contest rules, I found a set of coordinates no one else had noticed.
competition:2.cnHint: 零点在城市网格上发布了一场____，阿栗说这是个陷阱，但我在规则里发现了一串没人注意到的坐标。
competition:2.hook: The coordinates pointed to the building right behind me.
competition:2.line: 'This *competition* is not a game — it is a net,' Ali said.

sentences.en: Zero had posted a public *competition* on the city grid — a code-breaking contest, open to all.
Ali said it was a trap to pull every skilled hacker into the open.
sentences.cn: 阿栗说这是个陷阱，想把每一个有本事的黑客都逼出来。

sentences.en: Grey Crow agreed.
sentences.cn: 灰鸦同意了。

sentences.en: But buried in the contest rules, I found a set of coordinates no one else had noticed.
sentences.cn: 但我在比赛规则里挖到了一组坐标，其他人都没注意到。

farmer:2.en: The old man sitting by the canal did not look like a hacker. He wore mud-stained boots and called himself a *farmer* from the outer ring. But his fingers moved over the bench in a pattern I recognised — the tap-code Grey Crow had taught me on day one. I sat down beside him.
farmer:2.cnHint: 运河边那个自称外环____的老人，用手指敲出了灰鸦教我的暗语。
farmer:2.hook: He slid a folded chip across the bench without looking at me.
farmer:2.line: 'I am just a *farmer*,' he said, 'but I grow information.'

sentences.en: The old man sitting by the canal did not look like a hacker.
sentences.cn: 坐在运河边的老人看起来不像黑客。

sentences.en: He wore mud-stained boots and called himself a *farmer* from the outer ring.
But his fingers moved over the bench in a pattern I recognised — the tap-code Grey Crow had taught me on day one.
sentences.cn: 但他的手指在长凳上敲出了一个我认得的节奏——灰鸦第一天教我的敲击密码。

sentences.en: I sat down beside him.
sentences.cn: 我在他身边坐了下来。

female:2.en: Deep in the old port archive, I found a cracked data-chip. Its label read: 'Subject 7 — *female*, age unknown, last signal: Sector 9.' Ali leaned over my shoulder. The chip was warm, as if it had been held moments before. Someone had left it for us to find.
female:2.cnHint: 档案室里，我发现了一块破损的数据芯片，上面记录着一名____的信息。
female:2.hook: The chip's warmth meant the one who left it was still close.
female:2.line: 'A *female* agent — and her file has been wiped clean,' Ali whispered.

sentences.en: Deep in the old port archive, I found a cracked data-chip.
sentences.cn: 在古港的档案库深处，我找到了一块裂开的数据芯片。

sentences.en: Its label read: 'Subject 7 — *female*, age unknown, last signal: Sector 9.'
Ali leaned over my shoulder.
sentences.cn: 阿栗靠过来看我的肩膀。

sentences.en: The chip was warm, as if it had been held moments before.
sentences.cn: 芯片还是温的，好像刚被人拿过似的。

sentences.en: Someone had left it for us to find.
sentences.cn: 有人故意留给我们去发现。

holiday:2.en: The market square was bright with fake lanterns. Harbor City never rested, but tonight the billboards all flashed one word: *holiday*. It was a cover. Grey Crow had warned me that Zero used public festivals to move stolen data. I pushed through the crowd, eyes sharp.
holiday:2.cnHint: 广场上张灯结彩，但这场____不过是掩护行动的幌子。
